title: Journal groups entries by round number, so a round reset or out-of-combat mixes old and new entries
description:
User (2026-10-15): "log ordering. it is broken. since it's by turn number it gets messed up with we reset turns and go out of combat".

## Root cause
web/src/lib/groupByRound.ts buckets log entries by `entry.round` in a Map and sorts the buckets by round number descending (used by web/src/components/dashboard/CombatLog.tsx). After End combat / Set round to 0 / a round reset (ADR 0013 s5), new entries with round 1 (or 0) join the old round-1 group and sit below older, higher-round groups. The server order (action_log ORDER BY id DESC) is right; only the display grouping is wrong.

## Fix
Group consecutive runs in the server's order (newest first): a new group starts whenever the round differs from the previous entry's round. The same round number can appear as several groups. The current round's (possibly empty) group stays on top only if the newest entry is not already in it. Group keys must be unique (not the round number). Round 0 labelled as out of combat (existing turnLabel wording, check en+fr).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The journal is in strict newest-first order across round resets, End combat and Set round (vitest on the grouping: rounds 1,2,3 then reset then 1,2 gives groups 2,1,3,2,1 newest first; round 0 between combats).
- [ ] The empty current-round group appears on top only when the newest entry isn't in the current round.
- [ ] Filters (CombatLog filterEntries) still work with the new grouping.
- [ ] No new e2e spec; extend an existing one only if cheap (e2e < 5 min CI hard limit).
- [ ] just validate + just e2e green.

## Notes
UI only (display grouping), no review. Sonnet. Touches CombatLog.tsx which critical-kiv.23 (Fil sweep) also restyles: land this first.

title: Journal shows a multi-entry transaction as one group
description:
Since mic.3, one request may record several entries in one transaction (Next Round: the round advance plus the new initiative), and Undo pops them together, but the journal still lists them as separate rows, so it isn't visible that they undo as one. Suggested by the mic.3 developer.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Rows sharing a transactionId (GET /api/log) render as one group in the journal: visibly one unit, entries still readable, en + fr. Grouping is generic on transactionId, no per-kind code.
- [ ] Undone transactions show as undone as a group.
- [ ] Unit test of the grouping (web), screenshot folded into the existing round e2e; no new e2e spec.

title: Add UNIQUE(character_id) to active_buffs, spell_slots and round_state so state upserts work
description:
State upserts fail at runtime: the DAL saves for active buffs, spell slots and the round counter use `ON CONFLICT(character_id) DO UPDATE`, but migration 003_state.sql creates active_buffs, spell_slots and round_state with only `id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT` and no UNIQUE constraint on character_id. SQLite rejects every such upsert with "ON CONFLICT clause does not match any PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE constraint". Desired: each of the three tables holds at most one row per character, and the existing upserts work unchanged.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-12, autonomous; supervisor-confirmed evidence)
- Fix in the schema, not in the queries: add a NEW migration (next number after 005); never edit 003.
- The migration first dedupes existing rows per character_id, keeping the row with the highest id (the latest write), then adds a UNIQUE index on character_id for active_buffs, spell_slots and round_state.
- Remove the 9 `t.Skip("bug: upserts use ON CONFLICT(character_id) ...")` DAL tests added by critical-518.3 (PR #13, branch feat/518.3-backfill-tests) in buffdal (7) and spelldal (2) tests. Hence blocked by critical-518.3: stack on that branch or start after it is merged.
- NOT in scope: the nat-1 / nat-20 `t.Skip("bug?: ...")` in combatsvc tests (separate rules decision, handled by the supervisor with the user).

## Current behaviour
SaveActiveBuffs, SaveSlots and SaveRoundNumber always fail, which breaks Activate / Dismiss / Trigger buff, Next Round, Cast spell and Reset slots. Reproduced live (dev-518-6): POST /api/spells/0/cast on a fresh DB -> 500 "save slots: upsert spell_slots: ON CONFLICT clause does not match any PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE constraint".

## Key interfaces
- New migration file under the sqlite migrations dir, e.g. `006_state_unique_character.sql`: per table `DELETE FROM <t> WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT MAX(id) FROM <t> GROUP BY character_id);` then `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS <t>_character_id_uq ON <t>(character_id);`.
- The migration runner splits files on semicolons and executes statements one by one (no wrapping transaction), recording the file in schema_migrations only after all succeed: keep every statement idempotent and free of semicolons inside literals/comments.
- DAL query files (buffs.sql, spells.sql) and the BuffStore / spell-slot store ports stay unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] New migration exists; 001-005 are byte-for-byte unchanged.
- [ ] On a fresh DB, SaveActiveBuffs, SaveSlots and SaveRoundNumber succeed on first insert AND on a second save for the same character (row updated, still exactly one row).
- [ ] On a DB that already holds duplicate rows per character_id in any of the three tables, migrating keeps only the highest-id row per character and then creates the unique index (covered by a test that seeds duplicates before applying the new migration, or an equivalent migrate test).
- [ ] Re-running migrations on an already-migrated DB is a no-op (no error).
- [ ] The 9 buffdal/spelldal `t.Skip("bug: upserts use ON CONFLICT ...")` tests are un-skipped and pass.
- [ ] `just generate` run; any change in generated bob output (models/factory/queries) committed, and the CI generated-code check passes.
- [ ] Manual or HTTP-level check: POST /api/spells/0/cast on a fresh DB no longer returns 500.
- [ ] `just validate` passes.

## Tests
buffdal and spelldal DAL tests (the 9 un-skipped ones), plus a migration test for the dedupe-then-index path on pre-existing duplicates.

## Risky
Yes: migration on existing data (deletes duplicate rows) and buff / spell-slot / round-counter state semantics. Needs review per the workflow doc ("Migrations and DAL", "State integrity").

## Parallelism
Adds a migration touching active_buffs, spell_slots, round_state: do not run in parallel with another item adding a migration on those tables or changing bob generated output.

## Out of scope
- Changing the upsert queries or the store ports.
- The nat-1 / nat-20 combat skips.
- Merging the three tables or moving state into the characters table.

Take Critical from 'CI runs validate' to a repeatable, safe deploy. Local dev (just dev) and CI (just validate + generated-code check) exist. Missing: production-grade images, a hosting/auth decision, a fly.io app, automated deploys, backups, dependency hygiene.

Context: the PRD planned Proxmox + Tailscale (no auth, Tailscale as the security boundary). That was never set up; the user now leans towards fly.io. A public fly.io app changes the auth assumption: see the decision bead.

comments.author: moncef
comments.text: Postponed by the user 2026-10-12: focus first on an MVP usable at the table on Sat 2026-10-17. Note for 8g1.2/8g1.3: since critical-518.5, weapons.json is required at startup, so the image must ship seeds/.

title: Decide fly.io hosting shape: access control, topology, backups
description:
Decisions needed before any fly.io work. The PRD says 'no authentication, Tailscale is the security boundary'; a public fly.io URL breaks that.

Questions for the user:
1. Access control: (a) shared-secret/basic auth at the edge, (b) fly private networking + WireGuard/Tailscale only (no public ingress), (c) real login. Recommendation: (a) or (b); the app has no user model and is a single-character personal tool.
2. Topology: one container where the Go API also serves the built web assets (simplest on fly: one machine, one volume), vs. separate api and nginx apps as in docker-compose. Recommendation: single container.
3. SQLite on fly: single machine + fly volume (no horizontal scale, which is fine). Backup via fly volume snapshots only, or Litestream to object storage? Recommendation: snapshots first, Litestream if the data matters.
4. Environments: production only, or also a staging app deployed from PRs?
5. Budget/region constraints.

Output: decisions recorded in this bead's notes and in docs/ (an ADR-style note), then the dependent beads are un-labelled needs-info.
acceptance_criteria:

title: Run the Playwright e2e suite in CI (Chromium, artifacts)
description:
Run the Playwright e2e suite (`just e2e`, from critical-qki.16) in GitHub Actions on PRs.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-12)
- e2e stays local-only until this lands; filed as backlog under the deferred CI/CD epic so it isn't forgotten. Chromium only.

## Current behaviour
.github/workflows/ci.yml runs `just validate` and the generated-code check; no e2e.

## Key interfaces
- A separate `e2e` job (not inside `just validate`): setup Go/Node/just, `npm ci`, install Playwright Chromium (cached), `just e2e`.
- Uploads `web/e2e-results/` (HTML report, screenshots, traces) as a workflow artifact, always on failure.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The `e2e` job runs on pull_request and push to main, and passes on main.
- [ ] A failing spec fails the job and the artifact contains the trace and screenshots.
- [ ] docs/agent-workflow.md "CI and PRs" lists the e2e job.

## Out of scope
Firefox/WebKit; pixel-diff baselines; making e2e part of `just validate`.

Blocked by critical-qki.16 (the harness). Deferred with its epic: don't dispatch without the user's say-so.

title: probe
Visual identity: Critical! branding, primary/secondary/tertiary palettes, contrast
description:
User 2026-10-15, verbatim intent: the UI lacks contrast a lot. Primary palette for main elements, secondary for accents and highlights, maybe a tertiary for more accents; shades of each for depth and hierarchy. Modern and readable; tweak and improve the colour profiles. Green and red must translate correctly within the theme palette, play their role and stand out. There is a general lack of branding and identity: 'This is Dungeons and Dragons!! Not your accountant's spreadsheet.' The app name is nowhere: it is `Critical!` with the exclamation mark. Assign a Fable agent to the UX/UI design.

Builds on ADR 0017 (role tokens): the palette lives in the tokens, components keep using roles.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A design revision recorded as an ADR (supersedes/extends ADR 0017): primary/secondary/(tertiary) palettes with shade scales, semantic success/danger (green/red) tuned to the palette, contrast targets (WCAG AA for text), light and dark.
- [ ] The app name `Critical!` appears as a brand mark (header/title, favicon/page title).
- [ ] Applied across the app through the tokens; before/after screenshots of the main screens.
- [ ] e2e stays < 5 min; screenshots looped in existing flows.

title: Rulebooks reference: PHB + DMG as agent-readable docs in a private repo
description:
The user's request (2026-10-13, verbatim): "we should have the phb and the dmg in the repo in documentation in a format suitable for agents to refer to. ideally with some kind of indexing to avoid wasting tokens. what do you propose." Sources: https://archive.org/details/player-s-handbook-2nd-edition-2101 and https://archive.org/details/add2nddungeonmastersguidetsr2100

## Decided in triage (2026-10-13)
- ceffo/critical is PUBLIC and the books are WotC copyright, so no rules text goes into critical. The converted text lives in a separate PRIVATE repo, ceffo/critical-rulebooks.
- critical worktrees reach it through a sibling clone at the fixed path ~/code/critical-rulebooks (no submodule: `git worktree add` doesn't init submodules). critical gets only a `just rulebooks` recipe and a pointer in AGENTS.md / docs/agent-workflow.md.
- The supervisor creates the repo (`gh repo create ceffo/critical-rulebooks --private`) and pushes the private repo's work straight to its `main` after its `check` passes. No PRs in the private repo. The critical item is a normal PR.
- The raw archive.org OCR (`*_djvu.txt`, plus the PHB `_page_numbers.json`) is committed under source/. PDFs are fetched on demand by a script, never committed.
- INDEX.md: one line per chapter/section/spell/table PLUS every entry from both printed book indexes, each resolved to `term | book p.N | path`. Agents grep it, never read it whole.
- No seed-shaped spell export: the vodabois scrape stays the app's spell catalog source of truth. PHB spell files carry their stat block as frontmatter only.
- Books in scope: the PHB and DMG only. The layout takes another <book>/ later without rework.
- Not MVP (Saturday hard cut): P3, outside critical-qki.

## Private repo gate (instead of `just validate`)
A `check` script in critical-rulebooks: rerunning the conversion gives byte-identical output; every path in INDEX.md exists; every printed-index page resolves to a file; spot terms ("surprise", "THAC0", "Magic Missile") each give at least one INDEX line.

## Children
1 repo + script + sections + INDEX; 2 per-spell files; 3 hand-checked tables; 4 critical pointer + recipe.

title: Create critical-rulebooks: OCR source, conversion script, PHB/DMG section files, INDEX.md with the printed indexes
description:
Create the private repo ceffo/critical-rulebooks and a reproducible conversion of the PHB and DMG (archive.org OCR) into section-sized Markdown files with a grep-able INDEX.md. Read the epic for the decisions.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-13)
See the parent epic. The supervisor runs `gh repo create ceffo/critical-rulebooks --private`, clones it to ~/code/critical-rulebooks and gives the developer a worktree of it. The developer commits there and the supervisor pushes to main once `check` passes (no PR).

## Current behaviour
Nothing exists. Supervisor's sample of the archive.org `*_djvu.txt` OCR (PHB ~1.5 MB, DMG ~1.2 MB): the prose is clean. Problems: line-break hyphenation ("unerr- ingly"), stray quotes ("Tenser’'s"), running headers/footers and page numbers inline, tables mangled. Both books have a printed index (term -> page). The PHB item also has `_page_numbers.json`.

## Key interfaces
- Repo layout: `source/` (raw djvu.txt + page_numbers.json, committed as downloaded), `scripts/` (convert, fetch-pdfs, check), `phb/chNN-<slug>/<NN>-<section-slug>.md` (or `phb/chNN-<slug>.md` when a chapter is small), `dmg/...` the same, `INDEX.md`, `README.md` (how to regenerate, how agents should use it).
- Each section file: a few thousand tokens at most; starts with `# <heading>` and a line `Source: PHB p.N-M`. Split at the book's own section headings, keep the book's wording.
- INDEX.md lines: `term | PHB p.N | phb/...md` (sorted, one entry per line, no prose). It contains every chapter and section heading plus every printed-index entry of both books, each resolved to the file holding that page. Unresolvable entries go to a list in README, never dropped silently.
- Cleanup: de-hyphenate across line breaks (keep real hyphens), normalise quotes, strip running headers/footers/page numbers (record page breaks as `<!-- p.N -->` comments so pages stay resolvable).
- Tables: this item leaves them as the OCR has them, fenced and marked `<!-- TABLE: unverified -->`. Item 3 replaces them.
- `scripts/check` as defined in the epic.
- Language/tooling: anything that runs offline on this machine (Python 3 stdlib preferred); no network in convert.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Private repo exists with source/, scripts/, README.md; the source files are byte-identical to archive.org's.
- [ ] Running the conversion twice gives identical output (`check` proves it).
- [ ] Every PHB and DMG chapter is split into section files, none over ~4k tokens (check reports the largest).
- [ ] No hyphenation artefacts or running headers in a sample of 10 random files (listed in the handoff).
- [ ] INDEX.md resolves every section heading and every printed-index entry of both books; unresolved ones listed in README with the reason.
- [ ] `grep -i surprise INDEX.md` and `grep -i thac0 INDEX.md` each give lines pointing at existing files.
- [ ] `check` passes.

## Out of scope
Per-spell files (item 2), hand-checked tables (item 3), anything in critical (item 4), other books, seed data.

## Notes
Not risky (docs/tooling, no app code). Sonnet. No generated code in critical.

title: One file per PHB spell (Wizard, Priest) with stat-block frontmatter, indexed
description:
Split the PHB spell chapters (Wizard and Priest, Appendices) into one file per spell, with the stat block as YAML frontmatter, and add them to INDEX.md. Read the epic for the decisions.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-13)
- Frontmatter only; NO seed-shaped JSON/YAML export. The app's spell catalog source of truth stays the vodabois scrape (seeds/spells.json in critical); don't touch critical's seeds.
- Pushed by the supervisor to the private repo's main after `check` passes.

## Current behaviour
After item 1, the spell descriptions sit in the PHB appendix section files with the stat blocks as OCR prose.

## Key interfaces
- Path: `phb/spells/{wizard,priest}/<level>/<slug>.md`, slug = lowercase English name with hyphens (e.g. `phb/spells/wizard/1/magic-missile.md`).
- Frontmatter keys: `name`, `class` (wizard|priest), `level`, `school` (list; wizard) or `sphere` (list; priest), `reversible`, `range`, `components`, `duration`, `casting_time`, `area_of_effect`, `saving_throw`, `page`. Values copied as printed (strings), not interpreted.
- Body: the spell description, cleaned like item 1.
- INDEX.md: one line per spell, `<Name> (Wizard 1) | PHB p.N | phb/spells/wizard/1/magic-missile.md`. The printed-index spell entries now point at the spell file, not the appendix section.
- `check` gains: every spell file's frontmatter has every key; the count per class and level is reported.
- The appendix section files from item 1 either keep only the non-spell text, or are replaced by the spell files; no spell text appears twice.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every PHB Wizard and Priest spell has exactly one file; `check` prints the counts per class/level, and they match the PHB's spell lists (the per-level lists in the appendices). Mismatches are listed in README.
- [ ] Frontmatter is valid YAML with all keys for every file.
- [ ] `grep -i "magic missile" INDEX.md` gives the spell file; Priest "Cure Light Wounds" the same.
- [ ] Reruns are byte-identical; `check` passes.

## Out of scope
Comparing against critical's seeds/spells.json (a later item if the user wants it), French names (critical-qki.24), DMG magic items, tables.

## Notes
Not risky. Sonnet. Blocked by item 1 (needs the repo, the script and the cleanup).

title: Hand-checked PHB and DMG rule tables in tables/, indexed
description:
Replace the OCR-mangled rule tables of the PHB and DMG with hand-checked Markdown tables, verified against the PDF page images, in tables/, and index them. Read the epic for the decisions.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-13)
- Hand-checked against the archive.org PDFs (fetched by scripts/fetch-pdfs, never committed). Opus: verifying OCR tables against page images is fiddly.
- Pushed by the supervisor to the private repo's main after `check` passes.
- Chained after item 2 only because both rewrite INDEX.md; no real data dependency.

## Current behaviour
After item 1 the tables are left as OCR text, fenced and marked `<!-- TABLE: unverified -->`.

## Key interfaces
- `tables/<book>-<slug>.md`, one table per file: `# <Table N: title>`, `Source: PHB p.N`, a Markdown table, footnotes as printed.
- Section files keep a one-line link to the table file instead of the OCR table.
- INDEX.md: one line per table, `Table N: <title> | PHB p.N | tables/phb-....md`.
- `check` gains: no `TABLE: unverified` marker left among the listed tables; every table file is linked from INDEX.md.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] At least these tables are hand-checked against the page images: PHB ability score tables (Str, Dex, Con, Int, Wis, Cha), THAC0/combat progression, saving throws, XP and level progression per class group, spell progression (wizard, priest, bard), weapon tables (cost/weight/size/type/speed/damage), armour, movement/encumbrance; DMG attack matrices and saving throws, experience tables, magic item tables (random generation tables and XP/GP values).
- [ ] Every other table in both books is either checked or still carries the unverified marker, listed in README as unverified.
- [ ] The handoff lists each checked table with its page and any cell the OCR got wrong.
- [ ] `check` passes.

## Out of scope
Changing critical's seeds or rule_tables.json (if a mismatch with critical's seeds is found, report it to the supervisor for a separate item), other books.

## Notes
Not risky (no app code). Opus. Blocked by item 2 (INDEX.md conflict only).

title: Point critical's agents at the rulebooks: just rulebooks recipe and the INDEX-first usage rule
description:
Make the private rulebooks clone available to every critical worktree and tell agents how to use it cheaply. Read the epic for the decisions.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-13)
- Sibling clone at the fixed path ~/code/critical-rulebooks, shared by every worktree (no submodule).
- critical is PUBLIC: no rules text, no excerpts, only the path, the recipe and the usage rule.

## Current behaviour
No reference to the rulebooks; agents answer rules questions from docs/backend.md, the ADRs and memory.

## Key interfaces
- `just rulebooks`: clones git@github.com:ceffo/critical-rulebooks.git to ~/code/critical-rulebooks if it is missing, otherwise `git pull --ff-only`. Prints a clear message and exits non-zero without access (e.g. a public user without the private repo); it never runs as part of `just validate` or `just dev`.
- AGENTS.md + docs/agent-workflow.md (a short "Rulebooks" section; agent-workflow.md is where the agents read project specifics): for rules questions, `grep -i '<term>' ~/code/critical-rulebooks/INDEX.md` first, open only the file it names, never read whole chapters or INDEX.md whole. If the clone is missing, run `just rulebooks`; if that fails, say so instead of guessing the rule. The PHB/DMG text is a reference; the project's decided rules (ADRs in docs/adr, user rulings) win where they differ.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `just rulebooks` clones when absent and fast-forwards when present (try both by hand); it fails cleanly without access.
- [ ] AGENTS.md and docs/agent-workflow.md hold the pointer and usage rule above, no book text.
- [ ] `just validate` passes.

## Out of scope
The private repo's contents (items 1-3), any CI access to the private repo.

## Notes
Not risky (docs/tooling). Sonnet. Blocked by item 1 (the repo and INDEX.md must exist so the recipe and the grep example work). It touches different repos from items 2 and 3, so it can run in parallel with them.

title: chore: make web/ prettier-clean (just fmt-web reformats ~140 files) or drop the recipe
description: Found in critical-p3o.1: running `just fmt-web` reformats ~140 files, so the repo isn't prettier-clean and developers who format touch unrelated lines (prettier churn in cast.spec.ts on p3o.2). Either format the whole web/ once in a dedicated PR (no other changes, merged when no web branch is open) and add a prettier --check to `just validate`, or drop the recipe. Acceptance: `just fmt-web` on main is a no-op and validate fails on unformatted web files; or the recipe is gone and docs say so.
close_reason: Completed: web/ prettier-clean + check in validate (PR)

title: Unknown-AC attack card: hide 'Critique dès CA N' when no real AC can crit, and a way back to unknown after the AC was given
description:
Found while verifying critical-kiv.7 (unknown-AC attack, ADR 0012). (1) The tell-the-GM line shows critsFromAc even when it is far beyond any real AC (e.g. 'Critique dès CA 57'); the card should omit the crit part when critsFromAc is above the highest AC the rules allow (the bound comes from the server/ADR, not a TS constant). (2) Once the GM gives the AC there is no way back to 'unknown' on that attack.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The crit hint is shown only when a real AC can crit; the bound is server data or stated in ADR 0012.
- [ ] Decide (ADR 0012 note) whether an attack can return to unknown after the AC was given; implement if yes, latest-only like adjust.
- [ ] Unit tests; no new e2e unless a flow changes.

title: e2e attack.spec unknown-AC test assumes a crit hint; random critsFromAc > 10 fails main CI since #107
description:
Main CI run 38713686313 (b1ceb0a) red: web/e2e/attack.spec.ts:500 always expects 'A crit from AC N.' but since critical-ele (#107) the card omits it when critPossible is false (critsFromAc > 10). The value is random, so it passes or fails by roll. Fix: read critPossible from the roll response and expect the matching text.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The spec asserts the tell-GM text for both critPossible true and false from the response; no forced dice.
- [ ] just validate + just e2e green.

title: HP damage/healing source optional (hpsvc rejects an empty source; Moi column spec says optional)
description: The Moi column's damage/healing entry should allow an empty source (dashboard v3 spec), but hpsvc refuses an empty source, so the UI still requires one. Allow an empty source server-side (the log entry then has no player text; logSummary renders the kind from the payload), drop the UI requirement, test both. Found during critical-kiv.9.

title: Dice favourites: allow reordering (server-side order)
description: Found in critical-kiv.8: favourites are listed in creation order and cannot be reordered. Persist an order on the server (dice_favourites) and expose a reorder action. Needs a migration (review).

title: Moi column ChargeCards: show used/total ('N / M') like the timeline
description: Found in critical-kiv.18: the timeline now renders charge buffs as pips + 'N / M' from the served chargesTotal; the Moi column ChargeCards still show 'N charges'. Reuse the served left/total (unknown total -> today's text). UI only.

title: Spells panel filters spendable items client-side (type, not daily, count>0): serve eligible items from the server
description: Consume-item cast mechanic: the web spells panel re-implements the server's eligibility rule to list items. Expose eligible items from the server (spellbook info or an endpoint) and drop the client filter (no game logic in the frontend). Found during critical-rrv.

title: Player level on the name line, right-aligned
description:
User 2026-10-15: in the character card the level sits on the line under the name, wasting space. Put it on the name's line, right-aligned.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Level renders on the same line as the character name, right-aligned; long names truncate/wrap without overlapping it.

title: Concurrent pops (undo/void/reroll) from two tabs return 500 (SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT) instead of 409
description: SQLite WAL deferred transactions: two clients popping the same top at once both read it; the second's write upgrade fails with SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT -> 500. No double pop or corruption. Fix: BEGIN IMMEDIATE for pop transactions (actionlogsvc Undo/Void/VoidLatest, initiative reroll), or map busy to 409 centrally. Test with two concurrent pops. Found in the critical-kiv.2 review.

title: Spell lookup detail: serve damage dice at the Bard's level so the dice row can show them
description: Found in critical-kiv.12: the spell DTO serves no damage dice at the caster's level, so the lookup detail pane only shows dice rows for served values (duration, targets). Serve per-level damage dice from seeds on the server (no client computation); then show them in the existing dice row (To the dice / Roll). Related: critical-kiv.20 (spellbook DTO carries no dice text).

title: Phase 2 — Full Sheet
close_reason: Phase 2: Full Sheet is complete. Character attributes and saving throws are now persistent and rollable, and the 12,000+ spell database is fully searchable with metadata.

title: Dashboard v3: responsive combat dashboard redesign with Nocturne themes
description:
Redesign the main screen of Critical from the v3 design handoff (`.local/mockups/design_handoff_critical_dashboard/`), as a responsive dashboard rather than a pixel copy.

User's words (2026-10-14): "look at @/home/moncef/code/critical/.local/mockups/design_handoff_critical_dashboard/README.md prepare the work into tickets. note that the instructions say to adopt this pixel for pixel. this is not desirable. make sure this is still responsive design. we're not targetting mobiles screen size just yet but it should look good on a large high density browser as well. use /design-taste-frontend to guide you"

## Decided in triage (2026-10-15)
- Do it now, for the Saturday 2026-10-17 game: P1 items carry `mvp-saturday`. The first item (layout shell) redraws `docs/all.md` "Phase 1 Scope" (skill checks and XP ledger move in).
- Visual system: Nocturne tokens and the 6 ambiances (Arcane violet default), Inter + Phosphor icons (lucide and Geist removed), with the design-taste-frontend house rules applied (no gradients, no tiny tracked caps, tone steps instead of hairlines, tabular figures).
- Responsive: clamped columns, fluid type; 1280 to 2560 CSS px, full width at 2560 (no max-width). Mobile out of scope: no mobile items.
- Server returns structured data, never text; the frontend localises (en + fr). No client-side game logic or game state ("this thing will be multiplayer one day"). Per-device display prefs (language, light/dark, ambiance) stay in localStorage; dice favourites and the attack form's last choices live on the server.
- Undo = pop the newest log entry on the server (existing snapshot/restorer mechanism) with an expected-top id for concurrency; corrections as their own undoable steps come later (P2); no redo.
- Attack against an unknown AC: the server returns the AC hit and the crit threshold as data; the GM answers with the AC or Touché / Raté (no crit then).
- Initiative: plain 1d10 on Next Round, logged, poppable, rerollable. Weapon speed is out of scope.
- HP: floor at -10, server-side condition (ok / badlyWounded <= 25% / unconscious <= 0 / dead <= -10).
- Compétences in P1: bard skills and non-weapon proficiencies from the campaign sheet.
- No level-up: XP shows total, progress and ledger only.
- Character details are editable in the app.
- Rules stay as decided in the repo where the handoff differs: no special natural 1 / 20, crits per ADR 0001.

## Out of scope
Mobile layouts; level-up mechanics; weapon speed / initiative modifiers; redo; a client-side snapshot undo.

title: Lay out the v3 dashboard shell: responsive regions, rail, Nocturne themes and ambiances, settings popover
description:
Build the v3 layout shell and the theme system, and move the existing panels into it unchanged, so every later v3 item restyles one region.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-15)
- Nocturne tokens + 6 ambiances, light / dark / system, with the design-taste-frontend house rules applied (see common criteria). Arcane (violet) is the default.
- Inter and `@phosphor-icons/react`; remove lucide-react and Geist (one icon set, one family).
- Responsive from 1280 to 2560 CSS px, full width at 2560.
- Settings (language, appearance, ambiance) are per-device display prefs in localStorage.

## Current behaviour
`App.tsx`: Header on top, then a grid `1fr | 380px | 420px` (ActionArea | ResultCard | QuickHp + CombatLog). Theme: `lib/theme.ts` toggles `.dark` (key `critical.theme`); `LanguageToggle` (key `critical.language`); shadcn neutral tokens in `index.css`.

## Key interfaces
- Grid: rail | workspace (minmax(0,1fr)) | Fil column | Moi aside, under a full-width header region. Rail ~clamp(56px, 4vw, 80px), Fil ~clamp(340px, 26vw, 520px), Moi ~clamp(280px, 20vw, 400px) (tune, but clamped).
- Rail: Agir, Inventaire, Sorts (lookup) workspaces; active item marked; gear button at the bottom opens the settings popover. (Expérience is added by its own item.)
- Theme provider sets CSS custom properties on the root from (mode, ambiance): accent ramp 100-900 in OKLCH (lightness [.97 .93 .87 .78 .68 .58 .48 .38 .27] x chroma factors [.15 .3 .55 .85 1 .95 .8 .6 .4]), hue-tinted neutral ramp, background and surface; light mode reverses ramps; state colours (danger, heal, warning) keep readable lightness in both modes. Ambiances (hue / chroma): Arcane 289/0.125, Sylve 152/0.11, Sang 22/0.15, Ocean 240/0.11, Ambre 72/0.12, Obsidienne 265/0.014. Mapped onto the Tailwind v4 `@theme` tokens so shadcn components follow.
- Settings stored as `critical.settings.v1` = `{lang, mode, amb}`; the old `critical.theme` / `critical.language` values are read once as the initial value. "Système" follows `prefers-color-scheme` live.
- Existing panels placed: ActionArea in the workspace; ResultCard + CombatLog in Fil; Header identity/HP + QuickHp in Moi; RoundControl + BuffStrip in the header region (restyled later by their items).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The four-region layout renders with the existing panels working as before (existing e2e specs green, selectors updated where needed).
- [ ] Rail switches workspaces: Agir (current action tabs), Inventaire (InventoryPanel + WeaponsSection), Sorts (LookupPanel); state of each survives switching.
- [ ] Settings popover from the gear: language FR/EN, appearance Sombre/Clair/Système, 6 ambiance swatches; choice applies live and persists across reload; replaces LanguageToggle and ThemeToggle.
- [ ] All 6 ambiances x dark/light readable (screenshot each ambiance once in dark and once in light at 1440x900).
- [ ] Inter and Phosphor in use; lucide-react and @fontsource-variable/geist removed from package.json.
- [ ] ADR 0009 "Dashboard layout and theme system" (number reserved for this item): the region grid and clamp rules, the supported viewport range, the token/ambiance model, the house rules as adapted to Nocturne, where prefs live.
- [ ] `docs/frontend.md` "Dashboard Layout" redrawn (Mermaid) for v3; `docs/all.md` "Phase 1 Scope" updated: dashboard v3, skill checks and XP ledger are in; mobile still out.
- [ ] Common UI acceptance criteria below.

## Tests
Unit tests for the theme var computation (ramp values for one ambiance, light-mode reversal) and settings persistence/migration; Playwright: layout at the 4 viewports, settings change persists across reload.

## Out of scope
Restyling the panels themselves (each has its own item); the Expérience workspace; mobile.

Not blocked by anything; every other v3 UI item is blocked by it. Model: Opus (UI-heavy). Not risky (UI, docs).

## Common UI acceptance criteria (every Dashboard v3 UI item)
- [ ] Responsive, not pixel-for-pixel: the handoff's fixed widths (68 / 400 / 320 px, 1440x900, overflow:hidden) are intent. Columns use clamped widths, type and spacing scale (clamp on the root size); the layout holds from 1280 CSS px to 2560 CSS px using the full width (no max-width centring), with no stretched or empty look and no horizontal scroll down to 1024. Mobile is out of scope.
- [ ] One screen, no page scroll: each column scrolls on its own.
- [ ] Playwright spec(s) for the item's flows; screenshots at 1280x800, 1440x900, 1920x1080 and 2560x1440 listed in the report.
- [ ] House rules (design-taste-frontend skill, adapted to the Nocturne system, ADR 0009): no gradients (flat accent tint instead), no tiny uppercase letter-spaced labels (sentence case, >= 12px), surfaces separated by a tone step rather than hairlines, shadows only on things that float (popovers, menus), tabular figures on every number, at most 3-4 type sizes per panel.
- [ ] No game logic or game state in the client: the server returns structured data only (never display text); the frontend renders it with i18n.
- [ ] Every new string has a key in both `en` and `fr`; no French literals copied from the handoff; no new i18n tech debt.
- [ ] The handoff's placeholder sample data (character details, XP ledger, proficiency list, spell descriptions) is never seeded.

Design reference (not to copy): `.local/mockups/design_handoff_critical_dashboard/README.md` and `Critical Dashboard v3.dc.html` (logic in its `<script data-dc-script>` block; grep it, it is large). Where the handoff's rules differ from the repo's ADRs or from this item, the ADRs and this item win (e.g. no special natural 1 / natural 20; the effective THAC0 comes from the server).

title: HP below zero: floor at -10 and a server-side condition (badly wounded, unconscious, dead)
description:
HP below zero: floor at -10 and a condition computed on the server, shown on the HP block.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-15)
- User confirmed: HP stops at -10; the server returns the condition: ok, badlyWounded (<= 25% of max), unconscious (<= 0), dead (<= -10). Existing rule unchanged: HP never above hp_max.

## Current behaviour
HP is an append-only ledger, current = SUM(delta), capped at hp_max; nothing below 0.

## Key interfaces
- The HP ledger keeps appending events; a damage event that would go below -10 records the clamped delta (as the top cap does today), so SUM(delta) stays the truth.
- `GET /api/hp` gains `condition: "ok" | "badlyWounded" | "unconscious" | "dead"` and `floor: -10`.
- HP block: condition label when not ok; bar scale from -10 to max with a hatched "dying" zone below 0, "0" label at its boundary, max on the right.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ADR 0011 "HP below zero" (number reserved; may later fold into the HP ledger ADR): steps (1) HP never below -10 (clamped delta); (2) condition thresholds as above, evaluated on the server; one named test per step, failing on the old code.
- [ ] Undo of a clamped event restores the exact previous HP.
- [ ] UI shows the condition and the dying zone (e2e with relative values).
- [ ] RULES TRACE block in the report.
- [ ] Common UI acceptance criteria.

title: Compétences: roll non-weapon proficiencies (d20) and bard skills (d100) on the server
description:
Compétences tab: roll the Bard's non-weapon proficiencies (d20 at or under) and bard skills (d100 at or under) on the server, logged and shown in the detail card.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-15)
- In the P1 set (user: "include also proficiencies in new epic").
- Data from the campaign sheet (photo given 2026-10-15), checked against PHB Table 37; for "Musique DEX-1/WIS0" the user said: "take what you found in phb" -> Musical Instrument, DEX -1.
- Seed (ids are stable keys; display names are i18n keys in en and fr, never server text):
  - Non-weapon proficiencies (ability, modifier): musical_instrument DEX -1; tumbling DEX 0; ventriloquism INT -2; riding_land WIS +3; appraising INT 0; singing CHA 0; reading_writing INT +1; local_history CHA 0.
  - Bard skills (%): climb_walls 85, detect_noise 90, pick_pockets 50, read_languages 75 (sheet values taken as final, adjustments included).
  - Languages on the sheet (Elfique, Commun, Orque, Nain) belong to the character details item, not here.

## Key interfaces
- Tables + seed JSON for proficiencies and bard skills (migration; `just generate`).
- `GET /api/skills` -> `{proficiencies: [{id, ability, abilityScore, modifier, target}], bardSkills: [{id, percent}], last per id}`; target = ability score + modifier, computed on the server.
- `POST /api/roll/skill/{id}` -> `{id, kind: "proficiency"|"bardSkill", die: 20|100, roll, target, success, logEntryId}`; logged as `skill_check`, poppable by undo.
- Tab "Compétences" in Agir: rows are whole buttons: name | ability score and modifier ("DEX 17 −1") | target | last roll (✓/✗); bard skills: name | % | last roll. Detail card renderer for skill_check: die, "roll contre target", RÉUSSI / ÉCHEC.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ADR 0014 "Skill checks" (number reserved): (1) proficiency: d20, success when roll <= ability score + modifier; (2) a natural 20 always fails; (3) bard skill: d100, success when roll <= percentage; (4) each check is a logged, poppable entry. One named test per step (dice mock with distinct values, exact counts).
- [ ] Seed loads idempotently with the values above; en + fr names for every id.
- [ ] Tab, rows, detail card and journal entry work (e2e: roll one proficiency and one bard skill).
- [ ] RULES TRACE block in the report.

## Out of scope
Editing proficiencies in the app; proficiency slots / learning; thief-skill armour or race adjustments (sheet values are final).

title: Expérience workspace: XP ledger with the Bard +10% bonus and progress to the next level (no level-up)
description:
Expérience workspace: XP total, progress to the next level and an XP ledger with the Bard's +10% bonus. No level-up.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-15)
- Level-up is out of scope (user: "levelling up is out of scope for now"): no "Passer au niveau N" banner, the level stays the sheet's.
- Thresholds from PHB Table 25 (Thief/Bard): 12: 440,000, 13: 660,000, 14: 880,000, 15: 1,100,000, then +220,000 per level to 20: 2,200,000 (checked against the rulebook; the handoff agrees). Stored as rules data on the server.
- The +10% bonus eligibility (PHB: bard with DEX and CHA 16+) is decided on the server; the per-entry checkbox defaults to it.
- The XP ledger is outside the game action stack (own edit and delete), as in the handoff.
- Starting total: the seed's `xp_total` (1,293,418) becomes an opening ledger entry (or the base the ledger adds to); the handoff's sample ledger is not seeded.

## Key interfaces
- `GET /api/xp` -> `{total, level, currentFloor, nextThreshold, toNext, progress, bonusEligible, entries: [{id, date, session, reason, base, bonus, total}]}`; `POST /api/xp`, `PATCH /api/xp/{id}`, `DELETE /api/xp/{id}`; totals computed on the server.
- Rail item Expérience; Moi's "Barde · Niveau 15" opens it and shows the progress underline.
- Progress card: total large, "Avant le niveau 16 · N XP", bar with 10% ticks, level cells 13-20 with thresholds. Ajouter des XP: amount, reason, +10% checkbox, "Ajouter {total}" preview from the server (or a preview endpoint), Enter submits. Registre: in-row edit (Enter saves, Escape cancels).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ADR 0015 "Experience" (number reserved): (1) total = sum of entries (base + 10% when bonus, rounding stated); (2) bonus eligibility from DEX and CHA >= 16; (3) next level from Table 25. Named tests per step.
- [ ] Migration + `just generate`; ledger CRUD tests.
- [ ] Workspace, add / edit / delete flows (e2e with relative assertions).

Level-up (HP, THAC0, saves, slots); multi-class.

title: Make corrections (AC, save adjustment, GM verdict) their own undoable steps
description:
Make corrections (AC correction, save adjustment, GM verdict on an unknown-AC attack) their own undoable steps on the action stack, as the v3 handoff describes.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-15)
- Option (B) of the undo discussion: P2, after the basic server undo. No redo.

## Current behaviour
Corrections are audited amendments of an existing entry (`action_corrections.payload`); undo can only pop whole entries, so popping an attack drops its correction with it, and a correction can't be undone alone.

## Key interfaces
- A correction records its own before/after snapshot and sits on the stack; undo pops the newest correction first (restoring the entry's previous effective payload and any state it changed), then the entry.
- The undo tooltip names the correction ("Annuler : Correction CA 5 → 7").

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ADR 0010 amended with the correction step rules; one named test per new step.

title: Keep the e2e suite under 5 minutes on CI: one web server per worker, lean coverage rules
description:
User (2026-10-15): e2e must not become a bottleneck; the whole suite should run in a few minutes, especially on CI. Today: ~102 tests, 6.8 min locally with 2 workers, and every test boots its own API + Vite dev server (web/e2e/fixtures.ts), so the boot cost dominates. The dashboard v3 items would add more specs.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Vite (or a built bundle served once) is shared per Playwright worker; each test keeps its own API process and fresh temp DB (isolation unchanged), or an equivalent cheaper reset.
- [ ] Full suite under 5 minutes wall time on the GitHub Actions e2e job: an ABSOLUTE HARD LIMIT (user 2026-10-15), enforced by a job timeout so a slower suite fails CI. Aim well below it (headroom for the v3 specs still to come). Faster locally than today; timings in the PR.
- [ ] Coverage by risk, not by count (user: be smart balancing coverage and effort): list each spec with what it proves and its cost; keep what only a browser can prove (wiring, navigation, persistence across reload, one flow end to end), merge overlapping tests, move the rest down to Go or component tests.
- [ ] Prune: drop or merge e2e tests that only re-prove what Go or component tests already prove (rules math, edge cases, error branches). e2e keeps one happy path per user flow plus the screenshots.
- [ ] Viewport screenshots for the v3 layout live in one layout spec (all 4 viewports in one test), not one test per viewport per item.
- [ ] docs/agent-workflow.md Validation: the e2e budget rule (suite < 5 min on CI; e2e = one happy path per user flow; rules and edge cases belong in Go tests; a new spec must justify itself) so developers and reviewers enforce it.

## Out of scope
Pixel-diff baselines; other browsers.

Model: Sonnet. Not risky (tests/tooling). Should land before the bulk of the dashboard v3 items.

title: Undo the newest action from anywhere: server undo with expected top, Annuler button and Ctrl/Cmd+Z
description:
Global undo: an "Annuler" button and Ctrl/Cmd+Z that pop the newest action on the server, safe for several clients.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-15)
- Undo is the existing server action stack, not a client snapshot: popping the newest non-voided entry restores its "before" snapshots in one transaction (`actionlogsvc` Void / restorers). No redo.
- The request carries the id of the entry the client sees on top; if another action landed since, the server refuses (multiplayer later).
- Corrections (AC, save adjustment, GM verdict) becoming their own undoable steps is a separate P2 item.

## Current behaviour
`POST /api/log/{id}/void` pops entry id only if it is the newest (ErrNotLatest otherwise); `POST /api/hp/undo` pops the newest only if it is an hp_change. CombatLog shows Void on the newest entry.

## Key interfaces
- `POST /api/log/undo` body `{ "expectedTopId": number }` -> 200 with the voided entry (structured, as `GET /api/log` entries); 409 `{"error": ...}` when the top is not expectedTopId; 404/409 when there is nothing to pop.
- `GET /api/log` (or a field on it) exposes the current top id so the client can send it.
- Frontend: Annuler in the log/journal header; tooltip names the action ("Annuler : Attaque · Épée longue +2"), built from the entry payload in the frontend (lib/logSummary.ts); Ctrl/Cmd+Z triggers it except while focus is in an input/textarea/select; refreshes table state through `stores/table.ts`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Undo pops the newest entry of any kind and its whole effect is reverted (HP, buffs, round, ammo, slots, item charges), proven per kind by existing restorer tests plus one endpoint test.
- [ ] Stale expectedTopId -> 409 and nothing changes (test).
- [ ] Annuler button + tooltip naming the action; disabled when nothing can be popped.
- [ ] Ctrl/Cmd+Z pops; ignored while typing in a field (e2e).
- [ ] ADR 0010 "Action stack and undo" (number reserved for this item): the stack rule (user, 2026-10-14: "no amending values. just the note.. can only pop elements"), one transaction per pop, expected-top concurrency check, what is not covered (redo, popping corrections on their own).
- [ ] Common UI acceptance criteria.

## Tests
actionlogsvc: undo with matching / stale expected id (fails on old code: endpoint absent); handler test for 409; e2e: attack with ammo, Annuler, ammo count back.

## Out of scope
Redo; making corrections their own steps; client-side snapshots.

title: Write the type scale and density charter (ADR 0017) and apply it to the shell, header and Moi column
description:
Too much screen goes to oversized type and padding. User's words (2026-10-15): "so much space is wasted by humongous font sizes... what's the logic in there. don't you have a charter about font size? have an agent evaluate screen space usage and get some sanity in there." Write the charter (a type scale by role and a density rule) and apply it to the shell, the shared ui components, the header and the Moi column. The rest of the panels follow in the sweep items that depend on this one.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-15, user)
- More text and fewer pixels per glyph ("I expect to see more text and less dots"): the root font size is fixed at 16px. It no longer grows with the viewport (this drops the clamp in ADR 0009 step 3). Extra width goes to columns and content, not to bigger letters.
- Type can go below 12px: labels are 11px. This supersedes the 12px minimum in ADR 0009 step 5.
- Type scale by role (CSS px), one Tailwind token per role, and panels use only these:
  label/caption 11 · body/values/buttons/list rows 13 · panel title 14 semibold · key value (THAC0, dice, ability scores) 16 semibold · headline number (HP, turn, roll total) 24 semibold, at most one per panel. No `text-lg` or larger outside the headline token.
- Density: panel padding 12px; gaps of 4, 8 or 12px only; controls (buttons, inputs, selects, chips) 28px tall by default; primary actions (Attack, Next turn, Cast) 32px.
- Header: the turn block (turn number, status, Next turn, menu) and the effects timeline share one row, at most 64px tall (about 150px today).
- Measurable content target, checked in `layout.spec`.
- The user's table screen is a 5120x1440 ultrawide with Critical on a third of it: about 1707x1300 CSS px. It joins the layout viewports.
- Priority: now (P0), ahead of everything else.

## Current behaviour (audit, 2026-10-15)
- Root `clamp(16px, 0.3125vw + 12px, 20px)`: everything is 25% bigger at 2560 than at 1280.
- Turn number `text-5xl` (48px, up to 60), HP `text-4xl` (36px, up to 45), header about 150px tall (17% of a 900px-tall screen), Moi name `text-xl`.
- Shared components: button h-8/h-9, `text-sm`; input `text-base`; panels p-4.
- Classes used across `web/src`: text-sm 178, text-xs 72, text-base 13, text-2xl..5xl 14.

## Key interfaces
- ADR 0017 "Type scale and density", with numbered steps: root size, the role tokens, the spacing rule, control heights, header height, the content target. ADR 0009 steps 3 and 5 get "amended by 0017", and the ADR index is updated.
- Tailwind v4 `@theme` tokens in `web/src/index.css`, one per role (e.g. `text-label`, `text-body`, `text-title`, `text-key`, `text-headline`, each with its line-height). Pick the names in the ADR.
- The shared button, input, select, badge, label and card components move to the scale (default control 28px, `lg` 32px).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ADR 0017 is written and indexed; ADR 0009 steps 3 and 5 point to it; `docs/frontend.md` points to it for type and spacing.
- [ ] The root font size is a fixed 16px at every viewport.
- [ ] The role tokens exist, and the shell, header and Moi column (identity, abilities, HP block, HP change, saves) use only them. No arbitrary `text-[...]` sizes in those files.
- [ ] The shared ui components follow the control heights and the body size.
- [ ] The header is one row, ≤ 64px tall, at 1280x800, 1440x900, 1707x1300 and 2560x1440 (bounding-box assertion in `layout.spec`).
- [ ] At 1280x800, Moi shows identity, abilities, HP and all five saves with no column scroll, and the Agir weapon card is fully visible (bounding-box assertions in the existing layout test).
- [ ] 1707x1300 is added to the layout viewports with its screenshot. No new spec; the e2e suite stays under 5 min.
- [ ] `just validate` and `just e2e` are green. Other specs that relied on the old sizes are fixed.

## Out of scope
The other panels' sweeps (Agir, Inventaire, Sorts, Experience; Fil), which are separate items. Mobile. Any column-width change beyond what the header and the fixed root require.

## Notes
- Opus: this is a redesign that sets the charter the two sweeps follow.
- Not `risky`: UI and docs only.
- No generated code.

description:

## Decided in triage (2026-10-15)

title: Roll initiative (1d10) on every Next Round, logged, poppable and rerollable
description:
Roll initiative (1d10, lowest acts first) automatically on every Next Round, log it as its own entry, show it in the turn block, and allow a reroll.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-15)
- Plain 1d10, no modifiers. User: "speed will come later, not in scope".
- Rolled on the server through the dice port; its own log entry, poppable like everything else.
- Reroll = pop the initiative entry and roll a new one (server side, one call).

## Current behaviour
No initiative anywhere. `POST /api/round/advance` decrements buffs and logs a round_advance entry.

## Key interfaces
- Round state gains the current initiative (number, or none at turn 0 / out of combat), restorable by a restorer so undo reverts it.
- Next Round: after the round_advance entry, a separate `initiative` log entry `{round, d10}` is recorded (two entries: undo pops initiative first, then the advance).
- `POST /api/round/initiative/reroll` (name may differ, resource/action style): pops the current initiative entry if it is the newest and records a new roll; 409 otherwise.
- `GET /api/round` returns `initiative: { value, logEntryId } | null`.
- UI: turn block row "Initiative [value] d10 [reroll]" (tooltip: 1d10, lowest acts first); "Hors combat · l'initiative sera lancée" at turn 0; journal renders the entry from its payload; detail card shows it like a free roll.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ADR 0013 "Initiative" (number reserved): steps: (1) on Next Round, roll 1d10 through the dice port; (2) record it as its own log entry after the round advance; (3) lowest acts first (display only); (4) reroll replaces the newest initiative entry; (5) out of combat (round 0) there is no initiative. One named test per step, dice mock with distinct values and exact call counts.
- [ ] Undo after Next Round removes the initiative, a second undo the advance.
- [ ] Reroll refused when another entry is newer.
- [ ] Turn block shows the value and the reroll button; e2e covers next turn -> initiative appears -> reroll changes the entry.
- [ ] Common UI acceptance criteria.

## Out of scope
Weapon speed, casting time, DEX/reaction modifiers; group vs individual initiative options.

title: Every mutation is one transaction; undo pops the last transaction (redo later)
description:
Every mutation of table state is one transaction on the action stack; undo pops the newest transaction whole; redo (later) replays a popped one.

User's words (2026-10-15, answering whether p3o.4's ADR 0007 exception should stay): "adr 7 was trying to be defensive against out of order undos. the new rule we're going towards is: every mutation is transactional, we can reverse and pop last transaction (undo system) eventually support redo by replaying popped transaction"

## Audit (2026-10-15, scoper)
One request = one DB transaction + one poppable log entry with snapshots TODAY:
HP event, exposure, cast / receive, spell preparation, long rest (+ /api/spells/reset alias), buffs (activate, edit, dismiss, trigger), saved buffs (save, delete), round set / reset / pass-time, initiative reroll (void + new entry, one tx), attack / save / skill / dice rolls, corrections (adjust, verdict, unknown-ac: correction step + amend, ADR 0010 step 6), item create / edit / delete / use / restock, weapon create / edit / delete.

Non-conforming:
- Next Round: one DB transaction but TWO stack entries (round_advance + its initiative, ADR 0013 step 2): one gesture needs two undos.
- Per-panel / per-row undo paths beside the global undo: `POST /api/hp/undo` (pops only an hp_change on top, refuses with entry_not_latest otherwise, so an exposure on top cannot be undone from the HP panel) and `POST /api/log/{id}/void` (pops the top without expectedTopId).
- Outside the stack (not undoable): XP add / edit / delete (ADR 0015 step 4, edits leave no trace), character details PATCH, crit table PUT, dice favourites add / delete / reorder, attack form PATCH, note amend (`/api/log/{id}/amend`, ADR 0007 step 7).

Rules made obsolete or amended: ADR 0007 step 2 (only hp_change and the Bard's exposure carry an HP delta; the code is already generic: `actionlogsvc.Record` caps / floors any entry's HPDelta), step 3 (the app never works damage out, exposure the one exception), step 9 (HP panel undo); ADR 0010 step 1/2 (the unit popped is an entry, not a transaction) and the Consequence keeping `/void` and `/hp/undo`; ADR 0013 step 2 (initiative its own entry); ADR 0015 step 4 (XP outside the stack) pending the user's answer.

## Children
ADR 0018 first; one-undo and Next-Round grouping after it; scope of non-table mutations is needs-info; redo is backlog.
close_reason: Epic done: one transactional undo + redo

title: Write ADR 0018: every mutation is a transaction, undo pops the last one
description:
Write ADR 0018 "Every mutation is a transaction; undo pops the last one", amending ADR 0007 steps 2, 3 and 9, ADR 0010 steps 1-2 and its Consequences, and ADR 0013 step 2 where they conflict. Docs only, in the domain's words; numbered, testable steps per docs/adr/README.md.

User's words (2026-10-15): "adr 7 was trying to be defensive against out of order undos. the new rule we're going towards is: every mutation is transactional, we can reverse and pop last transaction (undo system) eventually support redo by replaying popped transaction"

## Decided in triage
- 2026-10-15 (user): every mutation is transactional; undo reverses and pops the last transaction; redo later, by replaying a popped transaction.
- 2026-10-15 (user, via supervisor): the p3o.4 exception (an exposure entry the Bard takes carries an HP delta, floor of ADR 0011, applied delta reported) stays, and is generalised: any transaction may change HP, through the same recording path (heal cap ADR 0007 step 4, floor ADR 0011 step 1).

## Current behaviour
See the epic's audit. The stack pops one entry at a time (ADR 0010); Next Round writes two entries; `/api/hp/undo` and `/api/log/{id}/void` are extra pop paths; ADR 0007 steps 2-3 say only hp_change (and the exposure exception) carry an HP delta although `actionlogsvc.Record` already handles any entry's delta.

## Key interfaces (to be stated in the ADR, implemented by the sibling items)
- A transaction = everything one state-changing request writes, in one DB transaction: one or more log entries plus their snapshots. It is the unit of undo.
- Undo pops the newest non-voided transaction whole (all its entries, newest first, restoring every snapshot's "before"), in one DB transaction, guarded by `expectedTopId` (ADR 0010 step 3 unchanged).
- One undo system: no per-panel or per-row pop endpoint; every undo button sends the global undo.
- Any entry kind may carry an HP delta; heal cap and floor apply in the recording path whatever the kind.
- Redo is reserved: a popped transaction stays voided; redo (later ADR) replays it; nothing in 0018 may make that impossible (keep the popped transaction's entries and snapshots).
- Mutations outside the stack: list them in Consequences as open, naming the needs-info sibling item's question (do not decide XP / details / crit table / favourites / attack form / notes here).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `docs/adr/0018-transactions-and-undo.md` (status accepted, dated) with numbered steps covering: transaction definition, undo pops the newest transaction whole, single undo system, HP delta on any kind, redo reserved, each step naming the test(s) the implementing items will add (test names may be marked "to be added by" with the step, not tracker ids).
- [ ] ADR 0007 steps 2, 3, 9 amended (status line "amended by 0018"), ADR 0010 (steps 1, 2, Consequences on /void and /hp/undo) and ADR 0013 step 2 (initiative in the Next Round transaction) amended the same way; the README index row for 0018 added and the amended rows marked.
- [ ] No code change in this PR.

## Out of scope
Code (sibling items); redo design detail (backlog item); deciding which non-table mutations join the stack (needs-info item).

Notes: model Opus (docs/agent-workflow.md: ledger/state semantics). Not reviewed (docs), the user reads the PR. Touches docs/adr/README.md, which critical-kiv.24 also amends (row 0017): trivial merge, not a blocker.

title: One undo system: HP panel undo and journal Void pop the newest transaction via the global undo
description:
One undo system: the HP panel's undo and the journal row's Void send the global undo (`POST /api/log/undo` with `expectedTopId`), so whatever is on top (an exposure, a cast, a buff) is popped from any of them. Retire `POST /api/hp/undo` and `POST /api/log/{id}/void`.

## Decided in triage
- 2026-10-15 (user): one undo system that pops the last transaction (see the epic).
- Proposed default (scoper, autonomous; confirm): keep the HP panel's undo button, now the global undo with the same tooltip as Annuler (names the action on top, `lib/logSummary.ts`); the journal row Void stays on the top row only and sends the global undo with that row's id as `expectedTopId`.

## Current behaviour
`/api/hp/undo` (`actionlogsvc.VoidLatest` with kind hp_change) refuses with 409 `entry_not_latest` when another kind is on top, e.g. the Bard's exposure, which changes HP but cannot be undone from the HP panel. `/api/log/{id}/void` pops the top without `expectedTopId`. Both are in `web/src/api/hp.ts`, `web/src/api/log.ts`, `stores/table.ts` (`undoHp`, `voidEntry`), `QuickHp.tsx`, `CombatLog.tsx`.

## Key interfaces
- Removed: `POST /api/hp/undo`, `POST /api/log/{id}/void` (handlers, routes, `VoidLatest` if unused, their i18n / render rows if unused).
- Kept: `POST /api/log/undo {expectedTopId}` → popped entry (ADR 0010 steps 1-4).
- Frontend: `undoHp` and `voidEntry` go through the undo store's global undo; table refresh as today.

## Acceptance criteria

title: Next Round is one transaction: group a request's entries so undo pops them together
description:
Group the entries one request writes into one transaction on the stack, so undo pops it whole. First and only multi-entry case today: Next Round (round_advance + the initiative rolled for the new round): one Annuler walks back to the previous round with its previous initiative.

## Decided in triage
- 2026-10-15 (user): every mutation is transactional; undo pops the last transaction (see the epic).
- Proposed default (scoper, autonomous; confirm): an initiative reroll is its own transaction; Annuler right after a reroll gives back the initiative rolled at Next Round; Annuler again pops the Next Round (round and initiative before it).

## Current behaviour
`buffsvc.AdvanceRound` runs one DB transaction that records two stack entries (ADR 0013 step 2): the first Annuler pops only the initiative, a second one the round. `RerollInitiative` voids the initiative entry and records a new one in one DB transaction.

## Key interfaces
- Schema: a transaction id on `action_log` (new migration, nullable or backfilled so every existing row is its own transaction; safe on existing data). bob regenerated.
- `actionlog.Recorder.Record` records into the current request's transaction (opened by the service's `InTx`, or a transaction scope the action-log port exposes); a correction step and its amend stay one transaction (ADR 0010 step 6).
- `GET /api/log` `topId` still names the newest entry; the undo pops every non-voided entry of that entry's transaction, newest first, restoring each snapshot, in one DB transaction (ADR 0010 step 4), refused as today on a stale `expectedTopId`.
- Wire: a log entry exposes its transaction id so the Annuler tooltip can name the transaction (the Next Round, not the initiative). The UI words it.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ADR 0018 step "transaction" and "undo pops the newest transaction whole": Next Round then one undo restores round, buffs and initiative to before it (composition test that fails on the old code).
- [ ] Reroll then undo then undo, per the decided default above (composition test).
- [ ] Rows written before the migration each pop alone (sqlite migration test on existing data).
- [ ] A restorer failing in the middle of a multi-entry pop leaves no void and no partial state (actionlogsvc test).
- [ ] `composition` `TestUndo_PopsEveryKindInOrder` updated: Next Round pops in one step.
- [ ] A table-driven composition test over every table-state mutation (the epic's audit list) asserts one undo walks the state fully back, so a future service that records two entries without the grouping fails.
- [ ] Annuler tooltip names the transaction's first entry (e.g. Next Round) (`web/src/lib/undoButton.test.ts`, en/fr).
- [ ] `just validate` green; `just generate` / `just mocks` output committed.

## Out of scope
Redo; mutations outside the stack (needs-info sibling); the per-panel undo endpoints (sibling, may land first; the two touch `actionlogsvc` undo code: not blocked, but not in parallel).

Risky: migration + ledger/state semantics (action stack). Review: yes, Opus (docs/agent-workflow.md). Model: Opus.

title: XP joins the undo stack; gameplay mutations are transactions, metadata is not
description:
XP joins the undo stack. User ruling 2026-10-15: "editing player metadata is not in the undo pipeline. gaining xp is. anything that mutates the state that affects gameplay."

## Rule (goes into ADR 0018's scope step, amending ADR 0015 step 4)
Every mutation of state that affects gameplay is a transaction on the stack and is undone by the journal's Undo. Player metadata and preferences are not.
- Joins: the XP ledger (add / edit / delete each one transaction; an edit keeps before/after in its snapshots).
- Stays outside: character details (race, alignment, age, languages…), dice favourites, the saved attack form, note amends on log entries, the crit table (a rules setting, ADR 0001).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ADR 0018 scope step amended with the rule and both lists; ADR 0015 step 4 amended (XP add/edit/delete are transactions, an edit keeps before/after). Tests named in the ADR exist.
- [ ] XP add / edit / delete each write one action-log entry with a restorer; the journal's Undo pops it and the XP total and level come back. Composition test per verb.
- [ ] The journal shows the XP entries like any other row (en + fr); one e2e happy path folded into an existing XP spec (add XP, Undo, total back).
- [ ] A scan of the API for any other gameplay-state mutation that writes no entry: list it in the PR; fix it here if trivial, otherwise report it.

Risky: yes (undo stack, restorers). Lands before Saturday.

title: Redo: replay the newest popped transaction
description:
Redo: replay the newest popped transaction (Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Z and a Redo / Rétablir button next to the journal's Undo), until a new transaction is pushed.

User's words (2026-10-15): "eventually support redo by replaying popped transaction". User 2026-10-15: lands before Saturday.

## Design (supervisor defaults from the scoper's proposals; written as ADR 0019, the user reads the PR)
- Replay = the popped transaction's entries are un-popped: their "after" snapshots are written back through the same restorers, in one DB transaction, recorded as a correction (the log stays append-only; no dice rerolled; ADR 0018 step 6 kept everything needed).
- Redo is guarded like undo: `POST /api/log/redo {expectedRedoId}`; refused (409) if the redo target changed since the client read it (multi-client).
- The redo stack is the run of popped transactions above the live top, newest pop first; it empties when any new transaction is pushed. Undo after redo pops it again; redo after redo replays the next one.
- HP: replay writes the recorded "after" (the pop order guarantees the state it was recorded against); no recompute.
- GET /api/log exposes the redo target (id + what it names) so the button tooltip names it (en + fr); hidden/disabled when nothing to redo.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ADR 0019 written (the design above), indexed; every test it names exists.
- [ ] Composition: for every mutation in TestUndo_OneUndoWalksEveryMutationFullyBack, undo then redo gives the state exactly as after the mutation (table-driven, extend that test or a sibling).
- [ ] Next Round: undo, redo -> round, buffs and initiative as after Next Round; undo ×2, redo ×2 in order.
- [ ] A new transaction after an undo empties the redo stack (redo answers 409/nothing to redo).
- [ ] Stale expectedRedoId refused, nothing changes; a restorer failing mid-replay leaves no partial state.
- [ ] Web: Redo button + Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Z, tooltip names the transaction (en + fr; unit test); one e2e happy path folded into an existing undo spec (undo, redo, state back).
- [ ] Generic: no per-kind code, no backend presentation strings, no tracker ids.

Risky: ledger/state semantics. Opus dev, Opus review.

title: Actor: remove db field, make pure value type
description:
Actor currently stores *sql.DB internally (actor.go:13), coupling the domain entity to persistence. Every Actor method (TakeDamage, GetHPState, ApplyBuff, etc.) is a thin wrapper that re-passes the same db to package-level functions.

Fix: remove the db field from Actor. LoadActor returns a plain struct with no DB reference. Callers (handlers) call the package-level domain functions directly — no Actor intermediary needed for persistence. Actor methods that are now pure (ApplyBuff, DismissBuff, TriggerBuff) keep their in-memory logic but drop the SaveActiveBuffs call; persistence is the caller's responsibility.

No new interface. No new abstraction. Just delete the field and its wrappers.

Files: api/internal/domain/actor.go, api/internal/handlers/*.go, api/internal/domain/buff_actor_test.go

title: ResolveAttack: pre-aggregate modifiers, decouple from Actor
description:
engine.ResolveAttack (combat.go) reaches into actor.ActiveBuffs mid-calculation to apply modifiers. This means: (a) buff state can diverge between LoadActor and the call, (b) the function does hit resolution + damage + crit + buff aggregation in one 60-line god function with no seam.

Fix: introduce a CombatContext value (pre-computed attack bonus, damage formula, crit threshold, buff modifiers). ResolveAttack takes CombatContext + DiceRoller, returns CombatResult — pure function. The caller (handler or a thin builder) aggregates modifiers before calling. engine/buffs.go ApplyBuffModifiers already produces BuffModifiers; caller computes CombatContext from actor.Stats + BuffModifiers.

Benefit: engine is independently testable without a DB-backed actor. Buff aggregation changes don't touch combat.go.

Files: api/internal/engine/combat.go, api/internal/engine/buffs.go, api/internal/handlers/combat.go

title: Handler boilerplate: extract CharacterContext value struct
description:
Seven handler structs each repeat {DB *sql.DB, CharacterID int64}. This is accidental width — the same pair exists by coincidence, not design.

Fix: introduce a CharacterContext struct (db, characterID) that handlers embed. Constructor: NewCharacterContext(db, charID). Handlers become e.g. type HPHandler struct { CharacterContext }. main.go creates one CharacterContext and embeds it into all handlers.

No interface. No behavioral change. Eliminates the repeated field pair and makes main.go construction obvious.

Files: api/internal/handlers/*.go, api/main.go

title: SaveCategory: move from engine to domain, decouple HTTP from engine types
description:
engine.SaveCategory is defined in api/internal/engine/saves.go but used directly in the HTTP request struct in handlers/rolls.go:21. This leaks engine internals into the HTTP contract — renaming or restructuring SaveCategory would break the API.

Fix: define a SaveCategory string type (or reuse engine's constants) in the domain package. The handler decodes the domain type; engine.ResolveSavingThrow accepts the domain type or the handler translates domain → engine before calling. The HTTP contract is decoupled from engine internals.

Files: api/internal/engine/saves.go, api/internal/handlers/rolls.go, api/internal/domain/types.go

title: Spell damage dice steps: per-round and per-instance dice that change (vitriolic sphere, chain lightning, incendiary cloud)
description:
Spells whose damage changes from one round, or one instance, to the next cannot be served today: the damage model (ADR 0008 step 8) repeats the same dice every round and every instance. Add a generic **dice step**: the dice of each round / each instance may differ, following the data.

Spells that need it (PHB via the rulebooks repo): vitriolic_sphere (round 1 (min(level,12))d4, half on a save; each following round two dice fewer while the target keeps failing a new save), chain_lightning (first strike (min(level,12))d6, then up to level-1 arcs, each one d6 fewer, each with its own save for half), incendiary_cloud (no damage rounds 1-2, then round 3 (level)d2, round 4 (level)d4, round 5 (level)d2; save to halve). Found in critical-5gy (PR #103), where they were left low confidence.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-15, autonomous scoping, user asleep)
- Split out of critical-p3o, one item per capability; priority stays P4 (backlog).
- Until this lands, chain_lightning and vitriolic_sphere stay low confidence (no dice served), unless the user rules otherwise (open question 1).

## Current behaviour
- `damage` has `dice` | `by_level`, `instances`, `rounds`; castsvc.rollDamage rolls the same dice instances x rounds times. DamageAt serves one instance's dice + instance and round counts.
- The three spells above are `confidence: low` (incendiary_cloud a `utility`), so nothing is served or rolled.

## Key interfaces (proposal, final shape decided in the ADR step)
- Data: either the formula grammar (api/pkg/formula) gains 1-based `round` / `instance` variables beside `level` (e.g. `(min(level,12)-2*(round-1))d4`), a dice count <= 0 ending the sequence; or a step table `by_round` / `by_instance` (like `by_level`). It must express all three spells above, including rounds with no damage (incendiary_cloud rounds 1-2) and a change of die size (d2/d4/d2).
- Served damage (DamageAt): the dice of every round / instance in order (a list of steps, each dice groups + constant + its round or instance number), not one repeated dice.
- Cast result and cast entry payload: every roll keeps its step (round / instance number), so the UI can show each and the GM can drop the steps a save ended.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ADR 0008 gains the dice-step step(s); each has one named Go test that fails on the old code.
- [ ] The loader accepts the new shape and refuses an invalid one at startup (dice multiplied/divided/capped stays an error, a step sequence with no damage at all is an error).
- [ ] vitriolic_sphere, chain_lightning and incendiary_cloud seeds use it and become `confidence: high` (`kind: damage` for incendiary_cloud), notes updated; their served dice at levels 12, 15 and 20 match the PHB (Go table test).
- [ ] A cast / spell received rolls exactly the served steps (dice mock: distinct values, exact call count per step).
- [ ] Spells without steps serve and roll exactly as before (existing tests unchanged).
- [ ] The spellbook / spell lookup and the cast result show each step's dice (UI, i18n en + fr); one e2e happy path at most (a lookup of a stepped spell), or none if an existing spec is extended.

## Out of scope
- Rolling the targets' saves, or stopping the sequence on a save: the app shows each step, the GM applies.
- vitriolic_sphere's 5-ft splash on secondary targets.
- Cast-time modes, partial saves, area-over-time exposure (sibling items).

## Tests / generated code
- Go: formula/loader tests, spelleffectsvc DamageAt tests, castsvc roll tests. No migration expected; `just mocks` if a port changes.

## Open questions (needs-info)
1. chain_lightning / vitriolic_sphere before this lands: serve the first hit's dice now, or stay low? (Default: stay low.)
2. Does a cast roll every step up front (as Melf's Acid Arrow rolls every round today), or roll only round 1 / the first strike and serve the rest? (Proposed: roll every step up front, each shown separately.)
3. chain_lightning: the number of arcs depends on how many targets there are; roll the maximum (level-1 or until the dice reach 0), or ask the player for the target count at cast time? (Proposed: roll the maximum.)

## Constraints (all items of this epic)
- Rules-engine work: Opus (developer and reviewer).

A new ADR, only if the design does not fit 0008, takes the next free number (0017; 0009-0016 are taken). Project ADRs win over the PHB (`~/code/critical-rulebooks`, grep INDEX.md first; never copy book text into the repo).

- No presentation strings from the backend: the API serves structured data (keys, numbers, dice); wording and i18n (en + fr) live in the frontend.
- No tracker ids in code, comments, test names or seeds.
