title: Write ADR 0023 (localized text: one row per language, no per-language field) and point every agent doc at it
description:
Write the localized-text rule once, as ADR 0023, and make every doc agents read point at it. Today no doc
states it: the hard rules only forbid composing text in Go (`fmt.Sprintf`), ADR 0021 prescribes
`name_fr`/`description_fr` columns and fields, and review checklist point 9 says the opposite ("stored book
text in a language is still presentation text"). Agents kept overriding the user's rule because of that
(#147 French stat columns, then `name_fr`/`description_fr`).

User, 2026-10-15: "we have ZERO localized text in the backend nor in the database. what is going on? why this
cardinal rule keeps being overriden? hunt and eliminate contradictions", then, once the data layout was
explained: "it's ok for the contents to be in the database but i would do it differently. name and
description do not hold the text but they hold a foreign key to localization table where you have one row per
language".

## Decided in triage (2026-10-15, user)
- The rule is about shape: **no column, field or property per language.** A text in a human language is a key
  into a localization table (`localized_texts`, one row per `(text_id, lang)`); adding a language adds rows,
  never columns, DTO fields or code paths.
- English is a language like any other: its texts are `lang='en'` rows, and `en` is the fallback language.
- Every human-language text column of reference data goes through the table: for spells `name`,
  `description`, `school`, `sphere` and the six stat texts (`casting_time` … `saving_throw`).
- One **generic** table for all reference data (items/weapons later), not one per entity.
- The API serves a language map per text field (`"name": {"en": "…", "fr": "…"}`); the client picks the
  language and falls back per field. No `lang` query parameter.
- Server-side name search stays, matching every language's name rows (language-generic).
- Own ADR, 0023 (ADR 0022 is the UI epic's, critical-uwtx.3).
- Mechanical enforcement in `just validate` (separate item).

## Current behaviour
- No doc states the rule. Contradictions found: ADR 0021 step 1 wording, "Consequences" (French name and
  description columns, "French names come from the catalogue's `name.fr`"), implementation notes "Storage",
  "REST", "UI" (`name_fr`, `/api/spells/names` with `name_fr`); ADR 0004 (buff names "from the catalogue in the
  player's language", fine in substance, cite 0023); `docs/agent-workflow.md` Hard rules (rule missing) and
  Review checklist 9 (wrong wording); `docs/all.md` "i18n: en/fr string keys for the UI and spell names (spell
  descriptions stay English)" (stale); `.claude/agents/supervisor.md` brief post-mortem paragraph (should cite
  the rule).
- `docs/backend.md` / `docs/frontend.md` describe the current `name_fr` columns and fields: those paragraphs are
  rewritten by the schema item, which changes the code they describe, not here.

## Key interfaces
- ADR 0023 "Localized text": the rule (shape, one row per language, en fallback, language map in the API,
  generic table, no per-language field anywhere: schema, DTO, TS types, catalogue artifact keys other than a
  language map), the user's words, what stays allowed (error `message` strings already excepted; text the
  player typed, e.g. character languages; source-language names recorded in journal payloads at write time,
  unchanged), and the search-cost reasoning (search joins only name rows by FK through the PK index; ~18k
  rows; an index on folded names is the next step if it ever grows, not a materialized view).
- `docs/adr/README.md` index row; ADR 0021 status line "amended by 0023" and a note at each contradicting
  passage pointing at 0023 (the "History" note keeps the record of `name_fr`).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `docs/adr/0023-localized-text.md` written as above, indexed in `docs/adr/README.md`.
- [ ] `docs/agent-workflow.md` "Hard rules for implementers": one bullet "**No per-language columns or
  fields.**" citing ADR 0023 and naming the check recipe (to come, critical item filed alongside).
- [ ] Review checklist point 9 cites that rule; the "stored book text … presentation text" wording is gone.
- [ ] ADR 0021 marked "amended by 0023"; each contradicting passage listed above points at 0023.
- [ ] `docs/all.md` i18n line corrected; `.claude/agents/supervisor.md` brief post-mortem cites the rule.
- [ ] `git grep -n -E 'name_fr|description_fr'` in `docs/` and `.claude/` only hits ADR 0021's history/notes
  and `backend.md`/`frontend.md` (left to the schema item).

## Out of scope
- Code, schema, API (the schema item). The mechanical check (its own item).

## Notes
- Docs only, not risky, Sonnet. Runs first; the schema item cites ADR 0023 steps.

title: Store spell texts in a localized_texts table (one row per language) and serve language maps instead of name_fr/description_fr
description:
Move every human-language text of the spell catalogue out of the `spells` columns into a generic
`localized_texts` table (one row per text and language), and serve language maps instead of `*_fr` fields,
per ADR 0023 (filed alongside; must be merged first). Removes the `name_fr` / `description_fr` violation.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-15, user)
See ADR 0023 (the docs item). In short: `spells.name`, `description`, `school`, `sphere` and the six stat
texts hold a foreign key to `localized_texts`, not text; English is the `en` row; one generic table; the API
serves `{"en": …, "fr": …}` per text field and the client picks with per-field fallback; server-side name
search stays, over every language's name rows. User on search cost: no materialized view; prove the query
uses the key instead (decided with the recommendation, 2026-10-15).

## Current behaviour
- Migration 027 added `spells.name_fr`, `description_fr`; `name`, `description`, `school`, `sphere` and the six
  stat texts are English text columns. The importer (`storage/sqlite/catalogue.go`, `catalogueadpt`) fills
  them from the artifact's `name: {en, fr?}` / `description: {en, fr?}`.
- `catalogue.Spell`, `spellsvc.Spell`, `spellsvc.SpellName` carry `NameFR` / `DescriptionFR`;
  `spellsvc` ranking matches `Name` and `NameFR` (`ranking.go`).
- REST: spell DTOs and `GET /api/spells/names` carry `name_fr` / `description_fr` (omitted without French).
- Web: `types/spells.ts`, `i18n/spellName.ts` (`spellTexts`, `spellName`), e2e fixtures and `lookup.spec`.
- The typed stats (`stats` JSON) are parsed at import from the English stat texts.

## Key interfaces
- Table `localized_texts(text_id INTEGER, lang TEXT, body TEXT NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (text_id, lang))`;
  `spells.<field>_text_id` (or the field name itself) references `text_id`. Exact naming is the developer's,
  constrained by ADR 0023 and bob (`docs/backend.md`).
- A new migration (031+) creates the table, moves existing values (en and fr rows), drops `name_fr`,
  `description_fr` and the text columns, and forgets `catalogue_meta` so the next startup re-imports (as 030
  did). Safe on an existing database: `spells` keys and every state reference (slots, buffs, journal) are
  untouched.
- Importer: one row per present language per field; an absent language has no row (never an empty body).
  The catalogue artifact format is unchanged (format 1; its `{en, fr}` maps already fit) and the rulebooks
  repo needs no change. The stats parser reads the `en` rows.
- Domain: text fields become a language map type (e.g. `map[string]string` or a small `Localized` type), no
  `*FR` field anywhere.
- REST: `name`, `description`, `school`, `sphere`, the six stat texts are `{"en": "…", "fr": "…"}` maps on spell
  payloads; `/api/spells/names` returns `[{id, name: {en, fr?}}]`. API contract change: `web/src/types` must
  match the Go structs.
- Search: ranks `q` against each language's name; the query joins only name rows by FK; page texts are
  loaded in one batched query, not one join per field.
- Web: `spellTexts` / `spellName` / `statText` pick `map[lang] ?? map.en`; the grey other-language name in the
  lookup heading reads the map. Behaviour unchanged for the user.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Migration creates `localized_texts`, moves existing en/fr text, drops `name_fr`, `description_fr` and the
  text columns; a migration test on a database holding 030's schema with French rows keeps every text and
  every key.
- [ ] No column, Go field, JSON tag or TS field named for a language remains (`git grep -n -i -E
  '(_|[a-z])(fr|en)\b'` over api/ and web/src, generated code included, finds none outside tests of the
  migration).
- [ ] Importer: a spell without French has no `fr` rows; a re-import that drops a French text deletes its row;
  importer tests of ADR 0021 step 5 still pass.
- [ ] Search matches English and French names with the same tiers as today (`TestSearch_RankingTiers`
  adapted); a committed test asserts with `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` that the name lookup in `localized_texts` uses
  its key (no full `SCAN localized_texts`).
- [ ] REST tests: language maps on spell payloads and `/api/spells/names`; a spell without French has no `fr`
  key.
- [ ] Web: `spellName.test.ts` and `statText.test.ts` updated; French and English lookup e2e stay green
  (`lookup.spec`), no new spec.
- [ ] `just generate` rerun and committed; `just validate` and `just e2e` green.
- [ ] `docs/backend.md` and `docs/frontend.md` paragraphs on spell storage and DTOs rewritten; ADR 0021
  "Storage"/"REST"/"UI" notes point at the new shape; ADR 0023 cites the tests.

## Out of scope
- Item and weapon names (their own item). Journal payloads that recorded an English name at write time stay
  as they are. Typed school/sphere enums. The mechanical check (its own item).

## Notes
- **Risky** (migration, API contract, domain structs across packages): review, **Opus**.
- Overlap, not a block: critical-uwtx.7 (spell lookup redesign) reads names through `spellTexts` /
  `spellName`. User (2026-10-15): run this item first so the redesign builds on the final contract; whichever
  merges second rebases. Also touches the same files as critical-y9e0.17 (parser version, re-typing at
  startup): not blocked, coordinate the migration number.

title: Check in just validate that no column, Go field or TS property is named for a language
description:
Enforce ADR 0023 mechanically: `just validate` fails when a language-named column, field or property comes
back, so the rule no longer depends on agents reading it.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-15, user)
"Hunt and eliminate contradictions" of the cardinal rule; agreed: a check in `just validate`, like
`just check-no-tracker-ids`.

## Current behaviour
- Nothing checks it; `name_fr`, `description_fr` and the six `*_fr` stat columns all got through review.

## Key interfaces
- A `just` recipe (e.g. `check-no-lang-fields`), part of `just validate`, committed and deterministic. It
  refuses, listing file and line: a migration column whose name ends in a language code (`_en`, `_fr`, any
  ISO 639-1 code the recipe lists); a Go struct field or JSON tag doing the same (`NameFR`, `json:"name_fr"`);
  a TS type property doing the same under `web/src`. Exemptions only by an explicit allowlist in the recipe
  (applied historic migrations 027/029/030 and their tests).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The recipe runs in `just validate` and CI's `validate` job.
- [ ] It fails on a scratch branch that adds `name_fr` to a migration, a Go DTO and a TS type (shown in the
  report), and passes on main.
- [ ] A test or a self-check proves each pattern (column, Go field/tag, TS property) is caught.
- [ ] ADR 0023 and agent-workflow's hard rule name the recipe.

## Out of scope
- Detecting French text in string literals (error messages, comments).

## Notes
- Blocked by the schema item (the check fails on today's `name_fr` until it lands). Not risky, Sonnet.

Sweep web/src for truncate/text-ellipsis/line-clamp and make each wrap or reflow. The UI redesign (scoper-ui) may supersede the layout; this item is the rule sweep.

title: Rework the screen around the focused activity: space by importance, no cut text, new brand mark
description:
The user, 2026-10-15 (verbatim): "I am still not satisfied with the UI layout and design language overall." "the space used on screen is not in adequation with the importance of the function. important information is often drown. it's correct to have a busy UI if there is some hierarchy in how information is prioritised. it's not good enough. the mockups that started the big rehaul are still a mile better. specifically the spells browser is barely usable. There should not be text that is cut and ellipsed because of bad layout decision. never ever ever. it's a big tell that the layout is wrong."

Reference: the v3 handoff mockup (`.local/mockups/design_handoff_critical_dashboard/`, not in the repo; open `Critical Dashboard v3.dc.html`).

## Decided in triage (2026-10-15, user)
- **Activity focus.** What matters depends on the activity at hand. The last result, HP and the turn with its effects are always visible in some form. The rest reshapes around the focused activity, roughly: act + dice + journal, spell lookup, XP. These groupings are not always mutually exclusive. Be creative.
- **Space, not type size.** The problem is how space is used (for example the left part of the header: brand, "Turn 8", initiative and Next turn spread over a wide, mostly empty band). No new big-number size rule.
- **No-cut rule.** At a reasonable canvas width, important text (names, values, journal text) is never cut or ellipsed. It wraps, or the layout gives it room. Cut text means the layout is wrong.
- **Spell names:** one name, in the UI language. The second-language name is dropped (never asked for). Search still matches both languages.
- **Mockup qualities to bring back:** visible section labels (CIBLE, POINTS DE VIE…), panel outlines and stronger contrast, the HP bar with its dying zone and colour thresholds, a calmer journal, more breathing room (14-16 px padding). The mockup's large numbers are welcome where the space allows, but no new size rule. Not wanted: the mockup's bigger buttons.
- **Journal:** one line per entry. The Note feature is removed entirely. Reroll shows on hover.
- **Draggable divider between columns:** dropped (a bad idea, per the user).
- **Brand mark:** "the critical logo is ugly." (user, 2026-10-15). Redesign the Critical! mark and wordmark (ADR 0020 step 5): options in the design item, the pick recorded in ADR 0022, built in the shell item.
- **Process:** design directions first (Fable), the user picks one, ADR 0022 records it, then one PR per area. Implementation is Opus by default; Fable when it shows a gain.

## Children, in order
1. Spell lookup names: a quick fix, independent of the design.
2. Design directions (Fable).
3. ADR 0022.
4. App shell, activity focus and header.
5. Then journal, character column, spell lookup, act panels with the dice composer, and XP (each blocked by 4).

title: Design directions: 2-3 whole-screen options (act, spell lookup, XP) and Critical! logo options, as static pages with screenshots
description:
Produce 2-3 **design directions** for the whole screen so the user can pick one before any implementation. They cover the dashboard, the act panels (Weapons, Spells, Items, Skills, dice composer) and the spell lookup. **Model: Fable** (user's choice, 2026-10-15).

Read the epic's description first (the user's words and every triage decision). Compare with the v3 handoff mockup (`.local/mockups/design_handoff_critical_dashboard/Critical Dashboard v3.dc.html`; "still a mile better" per the user) and the app as it is now (`just e2e layout`, screenshots in `web/e2e-results/screens/layout/`; with real data, `just dev` on `.dev/critical.db`).

## Decided in triage (2026-10-15, user)
- **Activity focus.** The last result, HP and the turn with its effects are always visible in some form. The rest reshapes around the focused activity: act + dice + journal, spell lookup, XP. These are not always mutually exclusive. The directions must differ in *how* they do this (for example explicit switching, automatic focus from what you touch, or panels that expand and collapse), and be creative.
- **Space before size.** Fix wasted space first. Example: the header's left part, where brand, turn, initiative and Next turn are spread thin. No new big-number size rule, but large numbers are fine where the space earns them.
- **Never cut important text** at a reasonable width (spell names, weapon and item names, journal text): it wraps or gets room.
- Spell names in the UI language only.
- Keep: visible section labels, panel outlines and stronger contrast, the HP bar with its dying zone and colour thresholds, a calmer journal (one line per entry, no Note, Reroll on hover), 14-16 px padding. Not wanted: bigger buttons; a draggable column divider.
- Keep the visual identity (ADR 0020: palettes, roles, Critical! brand) and the theme tokens.

- **Logo:** "the critical logo is ugly." (user, 2026-10-15). Show 3-4 options for the Critical! brand mark and wordmark (today a d20 face in `tint` with a `highlight` "!" plus a Cinzel wordmark, ADR 0020 step 5). Show them alongside the directions, at header size and at favicon size (16 and 32 px), in dark and light. The name stays `Critical!` with its "!" in every language. The logo choice is independent of the direction choice.

## Deliverable
- Each direction is a static page under `docs/design/ui-directions/<direction>/` built with the real theme tokens (`web/src/index.css`, the `themeVars` values) and real data samples. Use the Bard Kelsen Balstriel at level 15, real spells including long names such as "Detect Secret Passages and Portals" or "Comprehend Languages", a journal of about 15 mixed entries and 3 effects. Show each of the three activities.
- Screenshots of every page at **1707x1300** (the user's table viewport) and **1440x900**, in dark Arcane, committed next to the pages. Taking them is a committed, rerunnable script (house rule: no throwaway code), for example a `just design-shots` recipe that uses Playwright's Chromium.
- `docs/design/ui-directions/README.md`: per direction, a short rationale covering where each function lives in each activity, how the user switches, and how space is shared. Add a comparison table and links to the screenshots.
- No app code changes. No ADR (the next child writes ADR 0022 from the user's pick).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] 2 or 3 directions, each with pages for act (Weapons tab with a result card), spell lookup (with a long-named spell selected) and XP, plus the act Spells tab.
- [ ] Every page keeps the last result, HP and the turn with its effects visible in some form.
- [ ] No important text is cut on any page at 1707x1300 or 1440x900. The screenshot script fails if any element with text has `scrollWidth > clientWidth` while clipping.
- [ ] 3-4 logo options under `docs/design/ui-directions/logo/` as SVG, each shown in the header of at least one direction and at 16/32 px, dark and light.
- [ ] Screenshots are generated by a committed script; the README links them.
- [ ] `just validate` green (docs and script only).
- [ ] The PR body embeds or links the screenshots so the user can pick from the PR page.

## Out of scope
- Implementing anything in `web/src`.
- Mobile and widths below 1280.

## Notes
- The user decides by picking a direction (or a mix) on the PR; the supervisor records the pick on the ADR 0022 item.
- Not risky (no code).

title: Write ADR 0022: the picked design direction, activity focus, no-cut-text rule, brand mark
description:
Write **ADR 0022** recording the design direction the user picked from the design-directions item (named in its PR or noted on this item by the supervisor). It also records the house rule against cut text. Docs only. **Model: Opus.**

## Decided in triage (2026-10-15, user)
- House rule, in the user's words: "There should not be text that is cut and ellipsed because of bad layout decision. never ever ever. it's a big tell that the layout is wrong." Refined: "important text, given reasonable width of the canevas should not be cut."
- Activity focus: the last result, HP and the turn with its effects are always visible; the rest reshapes around the focused activity (act + dice + journal, spell lookup, XP), not always mutually exclusive.
- Spell names show in the UI language only. Journal: one line per entry, the Note feature removed, Reroll on hover. No draggable column divider. Bring back section labels, panel outlines and contrast, the HP bar dying zone and thresholds, 14-16 px padding. No bigger buttons.

## What the ADR states
1. **No-cut rule.** At every layout viewport (1280x800 to 2560x1440, ADR 0009 step 3), important text is shown in full: names (spell, weapon, item, effect, character), values, journal text, labels. It wraps or the layout gives it room. `truncate`, `text-ellipsis` and `line-clamp` are refused on it. Name the narrow exceptions, if the direction needs any (for example a horizontally scrolling favourites strip); each has a stated reason and the full text reachable without a hover. Also state how it is checked: a Playwright helper (for example `expectNoClippedText(region)`) used by `layout.spec`, and a review checklist line.
2. **Regions and activity focus**, per the chosen direction: what is always visible, the activities, how focus changes, and the column or space allocation per activity at 1440x900 and 1707x1300. This replaces ADR 0009 steps 1-2 where they differ.
3. **Space and type**: what changes from ADR 0017 (header budget, padding, any size role the direction needs). Amend or supersede ADR 0017 steps explicitly; no silent drift.
4. **Panel style**: outlines and contrast, section labels (sentence case or small caps, as picked; amend ADR 0009 step 5 if it changes the "no tiny uppercase" rule).
5. **Journal**: one line per entry, no Note, Reroll on hover.
6. **Spell names**: UI language only.
7. **Brand mark**: the logo option the user picked ("the critical logo is ugly", 2026-10-15). It replaces ADR 0020 step 5's drawing and, if it changes, the wordmark face. Mark ADR 0020 as amended.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `docs/adr/0022-<slug>.md` with Context (the user's words), Decision (numbered steps as above), Consequences.
- [ ] `docs/adr/README.md` index updated; ADR 0009, 0017 and 0020 status lines note what 0022 amends.
- [ ] `docs/frontend.md` "Dashboard Layout" points at ADR 0022. Fix only what is now wrong; the area items update the rest.
- [ ] `docs/agent-workflow.md` "Review" checklist gains the no-cut rule.
- [ ] Each later area item can cite a step of this ADR for each of its criteria.
- [ ] `just validate` green.

## Out of scope
- Code (the area items implement it).

## Notes
- Blocked by the design-directions item (its merge and the user's pick).
- Not risky (docs).

title: App shell: activity focus, always-visible result/HP/turn, header space and the new brand mark per ADR 0022
description:
Implement ADR 0022's **regions and activity focus** in the app shell. Covers what is always visible (the last result, HP, the turn with its effects), the **Critical! brand mark** (redesigned; the user: "the critical logo is ugly"), how the focused activity changes (act + dice + journal, spell lookup, XP), the space each activity gets, and the **header** rebuilt to use its space well. **Model: Opus** (UI-heavy), or Fable if the design item showed a gain (supervisor's call).

## Decided in triage (2026-10-15, user)
See the epic. Key points: the last result, HP and turn/effects are always visible in some form; the rest follows the focused activity; space before size (the header's left part is the user's example of waste); no draggable divider; never cut important text.

## Current behaviour
- `App.tsx`: a grid `rail | workspace | Fil | Moi` (ADR 0009 step 1). The rail switches the workspace only; Fil and Moi are fixed beside every workspace.
- Header (`Header.tsx`, `TurnBlock.tsx`, `BrandMark.tsx`, `EffectsTimeline.tsx`): brand, "Turn N", initiative, Next turn and ⋯ spread across the left; the effects timeline on the right; at most 112 px tall (ADR 0017 step 6).

## Key interfaces
- The workspace model in `lib/workspaces.ts` and `stores/` (or its replacement): whatever ADR 0022 names as the activity and the focus state. A workspace mounts on first visit and keeps its state (ADR 0009 step 2) unless ADR 0022 says otherwise.
- Region components stay plug-in slots, so the area items restyle their content without touching the shell.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Regions, activities and focus changes as in ADR 0022 (one criterion per ADR step the shell implements; cite the steps in the PR).

title: ADR: an item's own powers (STR trigger, effects, melee only), the Power Gem's thunder hammer first
description:
Write the rules for an item's own powers before they are coded: an item can carry effects that
apply while a trigger is met, like a buff that is never put on the list. The first case is the
Power Gem set in Kelsen's forehead: its thunder hammer form switches on by itself at effective
STR 18 or more.

User's words (2026-10-15): "the power gem is supposed to activate its powers when its user has
STR >= 18. what are we missing?"; "its powers on the weapon. the dispel magic once a day is
available regardless"; "the power gem is incrusted in the bards forehead. it's not going anywhere
without him dying. it's a powerful gem that normally is for warriors. but with magic the bard can
get to the strength requirement to have its power activate."

## Decided in triage (2026-10-15/16, user)
- The gem's powers live **on the item**, not as a buff on the list (no permanent buff to migrate
  or dismiss). `min_str` is a **trigger**, not an effect.
- One item, "Power Gem", with several powers. In now: the daily Dispel Magic (1/day, 10 m radius,
  no STR condition, as today) and the **thunder hammer**, triggered by effective STR >= 18.
  Trident of submission, the undead-destroying mace and the hammer's 30 m stun are not modelled
  (note only; backlog item).
- Thunder hammer = the weapon becomes +5/+5 and its raw damage dice are doubled; it keeps its own
  dice. Formula as already in ADR 0003 step 2 (user's own: "(((dice_value * 2 * enlarge_mult) +
  weapon_dmg_bonus) * crit_mult) + force_bonus"); no change to the damage math.
- "+5" vs the weapon's own magic: **the higher wins**, ADR 0002 step 6 unchanged (user: keep it).
- **Melee only**, as a generic effect condition (`weapon_kind: melee` or equivalent) any item power
  or buff can use; no gem special case.
- Shown **only while it applies**: below the trigger the item power appears nowhere (not on the
  effects timeline, not in the breakdown). At 18+ it shows under the item's name. Hand-made buffs
  with `min_str` keep today's dashed "needs STR N".
- The breakdown and timeline name the power from the item (by reference), so the French name comes
  with the item names' localization (critical-a1wm).
- Powers come from the seed and a data migration; no item-editor fields for powers now.

## Current behaviour
- ADR 0004 step 10 gates a buff's effects on `min_str`; the Consequences say "the daily gem item
  that activates them is inventory, not covered here". ADR 0016 items have no effects beyond
  effect dice/save, magic bonus and ammo kind.

## What to write
New step(s) in ADR 0016 (item powers: trigger, effects, how they join the buffs' aggregate, shown
only while applying, logged/voidable as item edits are), the melee-only condition and the item-named
modifier in ADR 0002 step 6 / ADR 0003 steps 4-5 and 11, and the ADR 0004 Consequences line updated.
Each new numbered step names the tests that will prove it (the implementation item adds them).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ADR text states every "Decided in triage" point above, one numbered step per rule, each with
      its planned test names.
- [ ] ADR 0004 Consequences no longer says the gem is uncovered; ADR index updated if a new ADR is
      used instead of amending 0016.
- [ ] No book text copied; `just validate` green.

## Out of scope
Code, the other gem forms, item-editor fields for powers, item name localization.

title: DM adjustment on skill checks: move the target, before or after the roll (API, ADR 0014)
description:
At the table the DM rules that a check is harder or easier ("this tumbling has an additional -2, so now it's DEX -2"). The player sets that adjustment before rolling or fixes it on the result card after the roll. The adjustment **moves the target**; the roll is never changed. Backend half; the UI is the next item.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-16, user)
- "we lack adjustments. the DM will specify that some feat is harder or easier and may say this tumbling has an additional -2 so now it's DEX -2." "the adjustment should be also on the result card, like we do for adjusting the AC for attacks."
- Same logic as the save adjustment (ADR 0006 steps 5-7: latest roll only, optional reason, amend correction, undoable, original verdict kept), but "it's not the roll that is modified, it's the target that is moved".
- It can be set **before the roll** (applies to that one check) and changed after on the result card.
- Sign: **+ easier, - harder**, app-wide. Proficiency: adjusted target = ability score + modifier + adjustment. Bard skill: adjusted target = percentage + adjustment, in percentage points.
- Ranges: proficiency -20..+20, bard skill -100..+100.
- A natural 20 still always fails a proficiency check (ADR 0014 step 2).

## Current behaviour
ADR 0014: no adjustment at all ("checks with a situational modifier from the DM" listed as not covered). `POST /api/roll/skill/{id}` takes no body. Payload `{id, kind, die, roll, target, success}` (+ ability, abilityScore, modifier for a proficiency).

## Key interfaces
- `POST /api/roll/skill/{id}` accepts an optional body `{"adjustment": n, "reason": "..."}` (empty body = 0, as today).
- `POST /api/roll/skill/{entryId}/adjust` `{"adjustment": n, "reason"?: "..."}`: same shape and refusals as `POST /api/roll/save/{id}/adjust` (400 out of range / reason > 80 chars / not a skill check, 409 not latest / voided), sentinel errors mapped centrally with i18n `apiError.<code>` keys if a new code is needed.
- Payload gains `adjustment`, `adjustmentReason` (omitempty), `adjustedTarget` and `rolledSuccess` (verdict as rolled with the pre-roll adjustment). Fields are added, never renamed; old entries decode with adjustment 0. `target` stays the unadjusted target.
- `GET /api/skills` last check carries the adjusted target and verdict in effect.
- Arithmetic only beyond the ranges: an adjusted target <= 0 always fails, >= 100 on a d100 always succeeds; no clamp.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ADR 0014 amended with numbered steps (pre-roll adjustment, post-roll adjustment on the latest check, audit as amend correction, ranges and sign); "not covered" line updated. One criterion per step below, each with a named test that fails on the old code.
- [ ] Pre-roll: the check is resolved against `target + adjustment`; exactly one die rolled (dice mock call counts).
- [ ] Natural 20 fails a proficiency check even with an adjusted target above 20.
- [ ] Post-roll: the verdict is recomputed from the stored roll and the new adjusted target; the roll never changes; a new adjustment replaces the previous one; 0 removes it and drops the reason; `rolledSuccess` is kept.
- [ ] Out-of-range adjustment (per kind) and a reason over 80 characters are refused (400); not the latest roll / voided (409); not a skill check (400).
- [ ] Each post-roll adjustment is an `amend` correction and its own undoable step (ADR 0010 step 6); undo restores the previous adjustment (composition test).
- [ ] Router wire-shape test for both endpoints; `web/src/types/skills.ts` mirrors the new fields.
- [ ] `just validate` green.

## Tests
skillsvc unit tests (table-driven, dice mocks), actionlogsvc amend tests for the new kind, composition undo test, router wire shape and error mapping. No migration expected (payload is JSON in the log); no bob regeneration unless a query changes; mocks regenerated if a port changes.

## Out of scope
The UI (steppers, result card): next item. Saves' own remodel: separate item. Persistent ("sticky") adjustments.

## Notes
Touches the amend path in actionlogsvc like the save remodel item: don't run them in parallel.

title: Skills tab and result card: DM adjustment steppers and adjusted target
description:
The UI for the DM adjustment of skill checks (the API comes from the item that blocks this one).

## Decided in triage (2026-10-16, user)
- "just dont put it on every line, find a clever way to add it." Chosen: **one stepper in each section's header** of the Skills tab: Proficiencies steps by 1 (-20..+20), Bard skills by 5 % (-100..+100).
- The pending adjustment applies to the **next check only** in that section and resets to 0 after the roll.
- While a section's adjustment is not 0, every row of that section shows the adjusted target with a small signed tag (e.g. `15` with "-2"), so the player sees the effect before clicking. The adjusted value displayed before the roll is a preview; the verdict and the logged target are the server's.
- "the adjustment should be also on the result card, like we do for adjusting the AC for attacks": the skill check result shows the adjustment and the adjusted target, and on the latest check a stepper + optional reason changes it (same interaction as the save adjustment row).
- Sign: + easier, - harder.

## Current behaviour
No adjustment UI for skills; the result card shows `roll vs target` and the verdict.

## Key interfaces
- Pending adjustments are UI state (not persisted, not sent until a roll); the roll sends `{adjustment}` with `POST /api/roll/skill/{id}`.
- Result card adjust calls `POST /api/roll/skill/{entryId}/adjust`.
- Journal line for an adjusted check words the adjustment (and reason) from the structured payload (`web/src/lib/logSummary.ts`), en + fr.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Each Skills section header has its stepper; rows of a section show the adjusted target and tag while its adjustment is not 0; it resets to 0 after a check in that section.
- [ ] Rolling with a pending adjustment sends it; the result card shows the original target, the adjustment (with reason) and the adjusted target, and the verdict.
- [ ] On the latest check the result card lets the user change the adjustment and reason; older checks show it read-only.
- [ ] Journal wording of an adjusted check in en and fr.
- [ ] No cut text (ADR 0022 step 1); the Skills region stays covered by `expectNoClippedText`.
- [ ] One happy-path e2e (adjust before roll, then adjust on the result card), justified in the report.
- [ ] `just validate` green.

## Out of scope
Backend (blocking item). The block layout and label contrast of the Skills tab (separate item; same file, so not in parallel).

title: Save adjustment moves the target, not the roll (ADR 0006 step 5)
description:
The save adjustment is modelled as a bonus on the roll (`d20 + buffs + adjustment >= target`). The user's ruling: "it's not the roll that is modified, it's the target that is moved." Remodel it so the DM's number moves the target, in the payload, the API and the display.

## Decided in triage (2026-10-16, user)
- The save adjustment moves the target. Same logic otherwise (ADR 0006 steps 5-7 stand: latest roll only, -20..+20, optional reason, amend correction, undoable, `rolledPassed`).
- Sign stays **+ easier, - harder** (app-wide convention): a -2 raises the save target by 2. Adjusted target = target - adjustment. The verdict is mathematically unchanged (`roll + buffs >= target - adj`).
- The display reads "d20 + buffs vs target 14 (-2)" style: the roll side shows only the dice and buffs.

## Current behaviour
Payload `{category, d20Roll, modifiers, target, rolledPassed, adjustment, adjustmentReason, total, passed, ...}` where `total` includes the adjustment. The result card and journal show the adjustment as a roll modifier.

## Key interfaces
- Payload fields are added, never renamed (the struct's own rule): add `adjustedTarget` and a roll total without the adjustment (name chosen by the developer, e.g. `rollTotal`). Old log entries carry neither; the API serves them in the new shape, computed on read in Go from the stored numbers (no log migration). The stored `adjustment` keeps its meaning and sign.
- `web/src/types` mirrors the change; the frontend never recomputes the verdict.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ADR 0006 step 5 (and its consequences) amended: the adjustment moves the target; one named test per changed step that fails on the old code.
- [ ] New saves log the adjusted target and the roll total without the adjustment; the verdict and margin are unchanged from today for the same numbers (table test incl. natural 1/20 plain arithmetic).
- [ ] An entry logged before this change (fixture payload) is served with the same verdict and the new fields filled.
- [ ] The result card and journal show the adjustment on the target side, en + fr; the adjustment row still works on the latest save.
- [ ] `just validate` green.

## Out of scope
Skill check adjustment (its own items, same convention). Attack AC adjustment (already a target).

## Notes
Touches the amend path (actionlogsvc) like the skills backend item and the result card like the skills UI item: run after them, not in parallel.
